(Section)

He swears by the scatterers (adh-Dhariyat), which are the winds that scatter the rain, scatter the dust, and scatter the plants when they become dry and crumbled, as Allah the Exalted said, ﴿so it becomes dry stubble, which the winds scatter﴾.

That is, they disperse and spread them. Then He swears by what is above them, which is the clouds: the ones that carry heavy loads (al-Hamilat Wiqran), meaning heavy with water. These are the water-skins of the earth, which Allah, glorified is He, drives over the backs of the clouds by means of the winds, as in the Jami' of al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of al-Hasan, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

"While the Prophet of Allah was sitting with his Companions, a cloud came upon them. The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said, 'Do you know what this is?'

They said, 'Allah and His Messenger know best.'

He said, 'This is al-'Anan (the clouds), these are the water-skins of the earth, which Allah, Blessed and Exalted, drives to a people who do not thank Him and do not call upon Him.'"

Then He swears, glorified is He, by what is above that, which is the ones that glide with ease (al-Jariyat yusra), and these are the stars that are above the clouds.

And ﴿yusra﴾ means subjected, made easy, and compliant. A group of the exegetes said that they are the ships that run easily upon the water, gliding smoothly.

Others mentioned no other meaning.

Our shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, preferred the first opinion, and said it is better in order and in progression from the lowest to the highest, for He began with the winds, above them the clouds, above the clouds the stars, and above the stars the angels: the ones who distribute the matter (al-Muqassimat amra), by the command of Allah which they were commanded, among His creation.

The correct view is that ﴿al-Muqassimat amra﴾ is not restricted to four.

It has been said that they are: Jibril, who distributes revelation, punishment, and various kinds of retribution upon those who oppose the messengers.

Mikha'il, who distributes rain, hail, snow, and plants, by the command of Allah.

The Angel of Death, who distributes deaths among creation by the command of Allah.

Israfil, who distributes souls back into their bodies at the blowing of the Trumpet. And they are (al-Mudabbirat amra).

Nothing in the wording indicates that these are exclusively them, and Allah knows best.

He swore by these four matters because of the lesson, the sign, and the manifest proof of His lordship, His oneness, and the greatness of His power. In the winds there are lessons: their blowing and their stillness, their gentleness and their violence, the difference of their natures and qualities, their directions, their turning, and the variety of their benefits, and the great need for them. For the rain there are five winds: a wind that spreads its clouds, a wind that gathers them together, a wind that fertilizes them, a wind that drives them wherever Allah wills, and a wind that scatters them before it and disperses them. For the plants there is a wind, for the ships there is a wind, for mercy there is a wind, and for punishment there is a wind, along with other kinds of winds. All of this requires the existence of a Creator who directs them, who manages them, who turns them as He wills, and who makes them gentle at one time and violent at another, merciful at one time and a punishment at another. At one time He gives life to crops and fruits through them, and at another time He destroys them through them; at one time He saves ships through them, and at another time He destroys them through them; at one time they moisten bodies, and at another time they melt them; at one time they are barren, and at another time they are fertilizing; at one time they are the south wind, at another the east wind (dabur), at another the breeze (saba), at another the north wind, at another hot, and at another cold. Yet, with their extreme strength, they are the most subtle of things and the most receptive of creatures to every condition, quick to be affected and to affect, gentle in their passage between heaven and earth. If they were cut off from the animals that are on the face of the earth, those animals would perish, like the fish of the sea which die if they are separated from water. Allah, glorified is He, holds them back when He wills and sends them when He wills. They carry sounds to the ears, scents to the nose, and clouds to the land of the dead. They are of the Spirit of Allah: they bring mercy, and from His punishment they bring chastisement. They are the strongest of Allah's creation, as al-Tirmidhi narrated in his Jami' from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "When Allah created the earth, it began to sway, so He created the mountains and set them upon it, and it settled. The angels marvelled at the strength of the mountains and said, 'O Lord, is there anything among Your creation stronger than the mountains?' He said, 'Yes, iron.' They said, 'O Lord, is there anything among Your creation stronger than iron?' He said, 'Yes, fire.' They said, 'O Lord, is there anything among Your creation stronger than fire?' He said, 'Yes, water.' They said, 'O Lord, is there anything among Your creation stronger than water?' He said, 'Yes, the wind.' They said, 'O Lord, is there anything among Your creation stronger than the wind?' He said, 'Yes, the son of Adam who gives charity with his right hand, concealing it from his left.'"

Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad, and al-Tirmidhi narrated in the story of 'Ad that He did not send upon them of the wind except as much as the ring of a signet, so it did not leave anything it passed over except that it made it like crumbled dust. Allah described it as ʿatiyah (violent, overpowering). Al-Bukhari said in his Sahih: it overpowered the guardians, so they could not turn it back.

The point is that the winds are greater than the signs of the Lord that indicate His greatness, His lordship, and His power.

(Section)

Then He swears by the clouds, which are among the greatest of Allah's signs in the atmosphere. They are of extreme lightness, then they carry water and hail until they become the heaviest of things. He commands the winds, and the winds carry them on their backs and move them wherever they are commanded. Thus they are subjected between heaven and earth, carrying the sustenance of the servants and the animals. When they pour it out where they are commanded, they dissolve and vanish by the power of Allah, for if they remained they would harm the plants and the animals. So Allah, glorified is He, creates them at a time suitable for their creation, gives them as much water as they carry, and drives them to a land in dire need of it.

Ask the cloud: who brought it into being after it was not, who carried water, hail, and snow, who carried it upon the backs of the winds, who held it between heaven and earth without a pillar, who gave relief to the servants with its rain and gave life to the lands with it, who turned it among His creation as He willed, who brought out that rain in a known measure and sent it down and then annihilated it after they had no need of it. Had He willed, He would have made it persist over them, and they would not have found a way to repel it. Had He willed, He would have withheld it from them, and they would not have found any way to reach it. If it does not answer you, then let the consideration of the One who sends the winds answer you: who created them by His power, directed them by His wisdom, subjected them by His will, and sent them as heralds before His mercy. He made them a cause for the completion of His blessing, and an authority over whomever He wills for His punishment. Who made them gentle and scattering, fertilizing, stirring, uniting, and nourishing the bodies of animals, trees, and plants, and made them shattering, violent, destructive, and overpowering, and other such attributes? Is this from themselves and their own essence, or is it by the management of a Manager, whose lordship all existing things bear witness to and whose oneness all created things affirm? In His hand is benefit and harm, and to Him belong creation and command. ﴿Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾.

Ask the ones that glide with ease, the ships: who held them upon the surface of the water and subjected the sea to them? Who sent to them the winds that drive them over the water as the cloud is driven over the backs of the winds? Who guarded them in their course and their anchorage from the rage of the water and the rage of the wind? Who fixed for them a wind of such measure that if it were increased it would sink them, and if it were decreased it would hold them back? Who made for them one wind by which they move, and did not give power over that wind to anything that would strike it or oppose it, so that it would surge in the sea to the right and the left, toyed with by the wind? Who taught the weak creature the craft of this great house that walks upon the water, crossing great distances and returning to its land, cleaving the water and ploughing it, going forward and backward by a single wind, running through waves like mountains? ﴿And among His signs are the ships running in the sea like mountains. If He wills, He stills the wind, and they remain motionless upon its surface. Indeed, in that are signs for every patient, grateful one. Or He destroys them for what they have earned, and pardons much﴾. Who carried in this house His prophet and his particular friends, and drowned all the people of the earth other than them?

Ask the ones that glide with ease, from among the stars, the sun, and the moon: who created them, perfected their creation, raised their places, adorned with them the dome of the world, and differentiated their shapes, measures, colors, movements, and places in the sky?

Among them is the large, among them is the small and the medium, the white and the red, the glass-colored and the pearl-colored, the one in the middle of the dome of the sphere, the one at its edges, and what lies between.

Among them is that which crosses the sphere in a month, among them that which crosses it in a year, among them that which crosses it in thirty years, and among them that which crosses it in multiples of that.

Among them is that which is never hidden and never sets in any state, so it is everlasting. Among them is that which is perpetually hidden, and among them is that which has two states, appearing and disappearing.

Among them is that which has two motions: a lateral motion from east to west and an intrinsic motion from west to east. So, as one star begins to set, another star is opposite it, another has risen and is ascending, another is in the eastern quarter, another is in the middle of the sky, another has inclined from the middle, and another has drawn near to setting, as if it were a watcher awaiting its disappearance with its rising.

If you reflect upon the states of these stars, you will find that they indicate the return (ma'ad) just as they indicate the origin (mabda'), and they indicate the existence of the Creator, the attributes of His perfection, His lordship, His wisdom, and His oneness with the greatest indication. Whatever indicates the attributes of His majesty and the descriptions of His perfection indicates the truthfulness of His messengers. Just as Allah made the stars guidance on the paths of land and sea, they are guidance on the paths of knowledge of the Creator, glorified is He, His power, His knowledge, His wisdom, the origin, the return, and prophethood. Their indication of these aims is no less than their indication of the paths of land and sea; rather, their indication to minds of this is clearer than their indication of the sensory paths. So they are guidance in this and in that.

(Section)

As for the indication of ﴿al-Muqassimat amra﴾, namely the angels: what is observed of the management of the upper and lower world, and what is not observed, is only through the hands of the angels. The Lord, exalted is He, manages the affairs of the world through them, and He has entrusted a group of them with each kind of work. He has entrusted to the sun, the moon, the stars, and the spheres a group of them; He has entrusted to the rain and the cloud a group; He has entrusted to the plants a group; He has entrusted to the embryos and the animals a group; He has entrusted to death a group; to the guarding of the children of Adam a group; to counting their deeds and recording them a group; to revelation a group; to the mountains a group; and to every affair of the affairs of the world a group. Along with this is what is in the creation of the angels of splendor and beauty, what is in them of strength and vigor, the subtlety of their bodies, the beauty of their forms, their perfect submission to His command, their standing in His service, and their execution of His orders throughout the regions of the world.

Then He swore, glorified is He, by these matters to the truthfulness of His promise and the occurrence of His recompense in reward and punishment, saying ﴿Indeed, what you are promised is true﴾, meaning that what you are promised concerning the Hour, reward, and punishment is a真 real and existing reality, and it is a promise of truth, not falsehood. ﴿And indeed, the recompense is surely to occur﴾, meaning that the judgment will certainly come to pass without doubt. It is permissible that "ma" be a relative pronoun with an omitted returning pronoun, the meaning then being "the thing you are promised is truly existing," that is, established and fixed; and that it be a verbal-noun particle (masdariyyah), meaning "your promise is true and sincere."

There is no need for the strained interpretation of making it mean "masduq" (that which is confirmed) in it; rather, it is truthful in itself, just as a speaker is described as truthful in his speech, so his speech is described as truthful.

This is like the sayings: "a concealing secret, a dark night, a fasting day, and gushing water."

And from it is ﴿a pleasing life﴾, and this is not a metaphor nor contrary to the requirement of the construction.

When you reflect upon this correspondence and connection between the thing sworn by and the thing sworn to, you will find that it indicates it and guides to it.

(Section)

Then He swears by the clouds, which are among the greatest of Allah's signs in the atmosphere. They are of extreme lightness, then they carry water and hail until they become the heaviest of things. Had He willed, He would have made it persist over them, and they would not have found a way to repel it. Had He willed, He would have withheld it from them, and they would not have found any way to reach it. Among them is the large, among them is the small and the medium, the white and the red, the glass-colored and the pearl-colored, the one in the middle of the dome of the sphere, the one at its edges, and what lies between.

Among them is that which crosses the sphere in a month, among them that which crosses it in a year, among them that which crosses it in thirty years, and among them that which crosses it in multiples of that.

Among them is that which is never hidden and never sets in any state, so it is everlasting. Among them is that which is perpetually hidden, and among them is that which has two states, appearing and disappearing.

Among them is that which has two motions: a lateral motion from east to west and an intrinsic motion from west to east. So, as one star begins to set, another star is opposite it, another has risen and is ascending, another is in the eastern quarter, another is in the middle of the sky, another has inclined from the middle, and another has drawn near to setting, as if it were a watcher awaiting its disappearance with its rising.

Along with this is what is in the creation of the angels of splendor and beauty, what is in them of strength and vigor, the subtlety of their bodies, the beauty of their forms, their perfect submission to His command, their standing in His service, and their execution of His orders throughout the regions of the world.

Then He swore, glorified is He, by these matters to the truthfulness of His promise and the occurrence of His recompense in reward and punishment, saying ﴿Indeed, what you are promised is true﴾, meaning that what you are promised concerning the Hour, reward, and punishment is a真 real and existing reality, and it is a promise of truth, not falsehood. ﴿And indeed, the recompense is surely to occur﴾, meaning that the judgment will certainly come to pass without doubt. Who made for them one wind by which they move, and did not give power over that wind to anything that would strike it or oppose it, so that it would surge in the sea to the right and the left, toyed with by the wind? Who taught the weak creature the craft of this great house that walks upon the water, crossing great distances and returning to its land, cleaving the water and ploughing it, going forward and backward by a single wind, running through waves like mountains? ﴿And among His signs are the ships running in the sea like mountains. If He wills, He stills the wind, and they remain motionless upon its surface. Indeed, in that are signs for every patient, grateful one. Or He destroys them for what they have earned, and pardons much﴾. Who carried in this house His prophet and his particular friends, and drowned all the people of the earth other than them?

Ask the ones that glide with ease, from among the stars, the sun, and the moon: who created them, perfected their creation, raised their places, adorned with them the dome of the world, and differentiated their shapes, measures, colors, movements, and places in the sky?

Among them is the large, among them is the small and the medium, the white and the red, the glass-colored and the pearl-colored, the one in the middle of the dome of the sphere, the one at its edges, and what lies between.

Among them is that which crosses the sphere in a month, among them that which crosses it in a year, among them that which crosses it in thirty years, and among them that which crosses it in multiples of that.

Among them is that which is never hidden and never sets in any state, so it is everlasting. Among them is that which is perpetually hidden, and among them is that which has two states, appearing and disappearing.

Among them is that which has two motions: a lateral motion from east to west and an intrinsic motion from west to east. So, as one star begins to set, another star is opposite it, another has risen and is ascending, another is in the eastern quarter, another is in the middle of the sky, another has inclined from the middle, and another has drawn near to setting, as if it were a watcher awaiting its disappearance with its rising.

Whatever indicates the attributes of His majesty and the descriptions of His perfection indicates the truthfulness of His messengers. (Section)

As for the indication of ﴿al-Muqassimat amra﴾, namely the angels: what is observed of the management of the upper and lower world, and what is not observed, is only through the hands of the angels. Along with this is what is in the creation of the angels of splendor and beauty, what is in them of strength and vigor, the subtlety of their bodies, the beauty of their forms, their perfect submission to His command, their standing in His service, and their execution of His orders throughout the regions of the world.

(Section)

He swears by the scatterers (adh-Dhariyat), which are the winds that scatter the rain, scatter the dust, and scatter the plants when they become dry and crumbled, as Allah the Exalted said, ﴿so it becomes dry stubble, which the winds scatter﴾.

That is, they disperse and spread them. Then He swears by what is above them, which is the clouds: the ones that carry heavy loads (al-Hamilat Wiqran), meaning heavy with water. These are the water-skins of the earth, which Allah, glorified is He, drives over the backs of the clouds by means of the winds, as in the Jami' of al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of al-Hasan, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

"While the Prophet of Allah was sitting with his Companions, a cloud came upon them. The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said, 'Do you know what this is?'

They said, 'Allah and His Messenger know best.'

He said, 'This is al-'Anan (the clouds), these are the water-skins of the earth, which Allah, Blessed and Exalted, drives to a people who do not thank Him and do not call upon Him.'"

Then He swears, glorified is He, by what is above that, which is the ones that glide with ease (al-Jariyat yusra), and these are the stars that are above the clouds.

And ﴿yusra﴾ means subjected, made easy, and compliant. A group of the exegetes said that they are the ships that run easily upon the water, gliding smoothly.

Others mentioned no other meaning.

Our shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, preferred the first opinion, and said it is better in order and in progression from the lowest to the highest, for He began with the winds, above them the clouds, above the clouds the stars, and above the stars the angels: the ones who distribute the matter (al-Muqassimat amra), by the command of Allah which they were commanded, among His creation.

The correct view is that ﴿al-Muqassimat amra﴾ is not restricted to four.

It has been said that they are: Jibril, who distributes revelation, punishment, and various kinds of retribution upon those who oppose the messengers.

Mikha'il, who distributes rain, hail, snow, and plants, by the command of Allah.

The Angel of Death, who distributes deaths among creation by the command of Allah.

Israfil, who distributes souls back into their bodies at the blowing of the Trumpet. And they are (al-Mudabbirat amra).

Nothing in the wording indicates that these are exclusively them, and Allah knows best.

He swore by these four matters because of the lesson, the sign, and the manifest proof of His lordship, His oneness, and the greatness of His power. In the winds there are lessons: their blowing and their stillness, their gentleness and their violence, the difference of their natures and qualities, their directions, their turning, and the variety of their benefits, and the great need for them. For the rain there are five winds: a wind that spreads its clouds, a wind that gathers them together, a wind that fertilizes them, a wind that drives them wherever Allah wills, and a wind that scatters them before it and disperses them. For the plants there is a wind, for the ships there is a wind, for mercy there is a wind, and for punishment there is a wind, along with other kinds of winds. All of this requires the existence of a Creator who directs them, who manages them, who turns them as He wills, and who makes them gentle at one time and violent at another, merciful at one time and a punishment at another. At one time He gives life to crops and fruits through them, and at another time He destroys them through them; at one time He saves ships through them, and at another time He destroys them through them; at one time they moisten bodies, and at another time they melt them; at one time they are barren, and at another time they are fertilizing; at one time they are the south wind, at another the east wind (dabur), at another the breeze (saba), at another the north wind, at another hot, and at another cold. Yet, with their extreme strength, they are the most subtle of things and the most receptive of creatures to every condition, quick to be affected and to affect, gentle in their passage between heaven and earth. If they were cut off from the animals that are on the face of the earth, those animals would perish, like the fish of the sea which die if they are separated from water. Allah, glorified is He, holds them back when He wills and sends them when He wills. They carry sounds to the ears, scents to the nose, and clouds to the land of the dead. They are of the Spirit of Allah: they bring mercy, and from His punishment they bring chastisement. They are the strongest of Allah's creation, as al-Tirmidhi narrated in his Jami' from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "When Allah created the earth, it began to sway, so He created the mountains and set them upon it, and it settled. The angels marvelled at the strength of the mountains and said, 'O Lord, is there anything among Your creation stronger than the mountains?' He said, 'Yes, iron.' They said, 'O Lord, is there anything among Your creation stronger than iron?' He said, 'Yes, fire.' They said, 'O Lord, is there anything among Your creation stronger than fire?' He said, 'Yes, water.' They said, 'O Lord, is there anything among Your creation stronger than water?' He said, 'Yes, the wind.' They said, 'O Lord, is there anything among Your creation stronger than the wind?' He said, 'Yes, the son of Adam who gives charity with his right hand, concealing it from his left.'"

Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad, and al-Tirmidhi narrated in the story of 'Ad that He did not send upon them of the wind except as much as the ring of a signet, so it did not leave anything it passed over except that it made it like crumbled dust. Allah described it as ʿatiyah (violent, overpowering). Al-Bukhari said in his Sahih: it overpowered the guardians, so they could not turn it back.

The point is that the winds are greater than the signs of the Lord that indicate His greatness, His lordship, and His power.

(Section)

Then He swears by the clouds, which are among the greatest of Allah's signs in the atmosphere. They are of extreme lightness, then they carry water and hail until they become the heaviest of things. So Allah, glorified is He, creates them at a time suitable for their creation, gives them as much water as they carry, and drives them to a land in dire need of it.

Ask the cloud: who brought it into being after it was not, who carried water, hail, and snow, who carried it upon the backs of the winds, who held it between heaven and earth without a pillar, who gave relief to the servants with its rain and gave life to the lands with it, who turned it among His creation as He willed, who brought out that rain in a known measure and sent it down and then annihilated it after they had no need of it. Had He willed, He would have made it persist over them, and they would not have found a way to repel it. Had He willed, He would have withheld it from them, and they would not have found any way to reach it. He made them a cause for the completion of His blessing, and an authority over whomever He wills for His punishment. Who made them gentle and scattering, fertilizing, stirring, uniting, and nourishing the bodies of animals, trees, and plants, and made them shattering, violent, destructive, and overpowering, and other such attributes? In His hand is benefit and harm, and to Him belong creation and command. ﴿Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 51, verse 7–9:

Then He swore by ﴿the sky, full of paths﴾.

The root meaning of ḥubuk (حبك) in the language is skilful weaving. It is said: "ḥabaka al-thawb" when he perfected its weaving; a "maḥbūk" rope is one that is very tightly twisted; and a "maḥbūk al-kafal" horse is one whose hindquarters are compact. Shamir said: al-maḥbūk in the language is that whose making has been perfected, and a "dābba maḥbūka" is one whose build is compact. Abu 'Ubayda and al-Mubarrad said: al-ḥabk is the path (ṭarīq), its singular being ḥibāk (حباك), and ḥibāk al-ḥamām means the streaks on a pigeon's wings, and ḥabk al-mā' means its path. Al-Farrā' said: al-ḥabk is the breaking up of anything, like sand when the wind passes over it, and still water when the wind passes over it; and the curling of hair is also ḥabk. Its singular is ḥabīka, like ṭuruq and ṭarīqa, and ḥibāk, like mithāl and mathal. What is intended by all of this is what Ibn 'Abbas expressed clearly when he said: he means good creation.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from him, saying: al-ḥubuk is its beauty and its evenness.

Qatada said: "possessing strong creation."

Mujahid said: "well-made construction."

He also said: "possessing paths," but they are far from the servants, so they do not see them, like the ḥabk of water when the wind strikes it, like the ḥabk of sand, and like the ḥabk of hair.

'Ikrima said: its construction is like the interlinked ornament (al-burd al-musalsal).

I say: In the hadith describing the Dajjal there is: "and his head is ḥubuk," meaning curly-haired.

Among the best of what has been said in the interpretation of (al-ḥubuk) is what al-Tirmidhi mentioned in his (Tafsir al-Jami') from the hadith of al-Hasan, from Abu Hurayra, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"Do you know what is above you?"

They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best."

He said: "Indeed it is the ar-Raqi' (the vault), a protected ceiling, and a restrained wave."

And he mentioned the hadith.

(Section)

Then He mentioned what was sworn to, saying: ﴿Indeed you are in a discordant saying. Turned away from it is whoever is turned away.﴾

So the "discordant saying" is their statements concerning the Qur'an and concerning the Prophet, and all of it is conjecture (kharṣ), for when they denied the truth, their doctrines, opinions, paths and sayings became divergent. Indeed the truth is one thing and a straight path, so whoever opposes it finds paths and doctrines diverging, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Rather, they denied the truth when it came to them, so they are in a confused matter.﴾

That is, mixed up and confused.

Included in this answer is that you are in false, contradictory statements, some of which refute others.

Then He, glorified be He, informed that, because of their denial of the truth, whoever is turned away from this discordant saying is turned away by means of it. So "ʿan" (عن) here contains a sense of causation, like His saying: ﴿We will not abandon our gods because of your saying (ʿan qawlika)﴾.

And His saying ﴿whoever is turned away (man ufik)﴾ means whoever was predestined in Allah's knowledge to be led astray and turned away, like His saying: ﴿Indeed you and what you worship are not able to tempt [anyone] against Him, except him who is destined for the Blazing Fire.﴾

A group said: the pronoun refers to the Qur'an.

It was said: to faith.

It was said: to the Messenger.

And the meaning is: whoever is turned away from it is turned away until he denies it.

It was said: to the Messenger.

And the meaning is: whoever is turned away from it is turned away until he denies it.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 51, verse 10–11:

When this divergent saying was mere conjecture and falsehood, He said, ﴿Killed be the conjecturers﴾, that is, the deniers,

﴿who are in heedlessness, inattentive﴾, and in ignorance that has overwhelmed their hearts, that is, covered and enveloped them, like the overwhelming of water and the overwhelming of death.

So the "overwhelmings" (ghamarat) are whatever covers the heart of ignorance, or desire, or intoxication, or heedlessness, or love, or hatred, or fear, or grief, and the like. The Exalted said, ﴿Nay, their hearts are in heedlessness of this﴾, meaning heedlessness.

It was also said: ignorance.

Then He described them as being inattentive within their heedlessness. Sahw (inattentiveness) is being unmindful of a thing and the heart departing from it. The difference between it and nisyan (forgetting) is that nisyan is heedlessness after remembrance and knowledge, whereas sahw does not necessarily entail that.

(Benefit)

The root of khars is speech without knowledge, rather based on conjecture, estimation, and throwing out words without proof of their soundness. From this, the liar is called a kharrash (conjecturer), and the one who holds conjecture and estimation is called a kharrash.

(Section)

As for the ghamarat, they are the plural of ghamra, and ghamra is what overwhelms the heart of love, intoxication, or heedlessness. God the Exalted said, ﴿Killed be the conjecturers, who are in heedlessness, inattentive﴾.

That is, in heedlessness that has overwhelmed their hearts.

And He the Exalted said, ﴿So leave them in their heedlessness for a time﴾.

From it comes al-ma' al-ghamr, the abundant water that covers whoever enters it, and from it come the ghamarat of death, that is, its severities.

Likewise the ghamarat of love, which covers the heart of the lover and overwhelms it.

From it is their saying, "a man of ghamr al-rida'" (one whose cloak overwhelms), a metaphor for generosity, because he overwhelms faults, that is, covers them, so no fault appears alongside generosity.

He said:

And al-Qatami, describing Noah's ship, said:

"Until it reached al-Judi and became a stone ∗∗∗ and that ghamr had receded"

That is, the water that overwhelmed the earth and whoever was upon it.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 51, verses 13–14:

Then He said, ﴿They ask, "When is the Day of Judgment?"﴾ out of disbelief in its occurrence and denial of it.

Then the Most High informed that it will be ﴿the Day they are tried over the Fire﴾.

The well-known explanation of this word is that it means "they will be burned." However, the word (ʿalā, "over") conveys an additional meaning beyond what they have mentioned. If the intended meaning were the burning itself, it would have said "their day, they will be tried in the Fire."

Because of this, when these scholars recognized that, many of them said that (ʿalā) carries the meaning of (fī, "in"), just as (fī) can carry the meaning of (ʿalā).

The apparent meaning is that their trial is over the Fire.

It has been said that their trial in it is for them when they are presented to it and stand over it, a trial; and when they enter it and are punished by it, a trial even greater than that.

Whoever takes the trial here to mean burning derives it from His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who tried the believing men and believing women and then did not repent...﴾

He also cited in support of this the use of this same word in Surah adh-Dhariyat.

The reality of the matter is that fitnah (trial, affliction) is applied to punishment and to its cause. For this reason Allah called disbelief a fitnah. Since they brought about the fitnah, which is the cause of punishment in the world, He called their recompense a fitnah. For this reason He said: ﴿Taste your fitnah﴾.

Their standing over the Fire and their being presented to it is among the greatest of their trials, and the last of this trial is entering the Fire and being punished by it.

They were tried first by the causes of worldly life and its adornments, then they were tried by the sending of messengers to them, then they were tried by opposing and denying them, then they were tried by the punishment of the world, then they were tried by the punishment of death, then they will be tried at the standing place of the Resurrection, then when they are gathered to the Fire they will stand over it and be presented to it.

That is among the greatest of their trials, and then the greatest trial, which makes them forget all the trials before it.

(Section: The reality of fitnah)

Its reality is that it is the shirk (association of partners with Allah) which its bearer calls others to and fights for, and punishes whoever is not tried by it. For this reason it is said to them at the time of their punishment by the Fire and their trial by it: ﴿Taste your fitnah﴾.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Your denial."

Its reality is: taste the end of your trial, its outcome, and the final result of your affair, as in His saying: ﴿Taste what you used to earn﴾ [az-Zumar: 24].

Just as they tried His servants into shirk, they are tried by the Fire, and it is said to them: "Taste your fitnah." From this is His saying, the Most High: ﴿Indeed, those who tried the believing men and believing women and then did not repent...﴾ [al-Buruj: 10].

The fitnah here has been explained as their torturing the believers and burning them with fire, while the word is more general than that.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 51, verses 17–18:

Then he mentioned their night, and that their sleep during it was little.

It has been said that (ma) is negative, and the meaning is: "They used to sleep but little of the night, so how much less of it?"

But this is weak, for several reasons:

The first is that this is not necessarily implied by the description of the God-fearing (al-muttaqun), who deserve this reward.

The second is that standing in prayer during half of the night, while sleeping the other half, is more beloved to God than standing in prayer for the whole night.

The third is that if the intended meaning were to keep vigil through the entire night, the person most entitled to this would be the Messenger of God (ﷺ), yet he never stood in prayer all night until morning.

The fourth is that God, exalted is He, commanded His Messenger to pray with the Qur'an during part of the night, not throughout the whole night. He said: ﴿And during part of the night, pray with it﴾.

The fifth is that when He commanded him to stand in prayer at night in the surah al-Muzzammil, He commanded him to stand for half of it, or a little less than half, or a little more than half. He mentioned these three degrees and did not mention standing for the whole night.

The sixth is that when the Prophet (ﷺ) was informed about ʿUthman ibn Maẓʿun, that he did not sleep at night, he sent for him. He came, and the Prophet said:

"O ʿUthman, have you turned away from my Sunnah?"

He said: "No, by God, O Messenger of God, but I seek your Sunnah."

He said: "I sleep, and I pray, and I fast and break my fast, and I marry women. So fear God, O ʿUthman, for your family has a right over you, your guest has a right over you, and your self has a right over you. So fast and break your fast, pray and sleep."

And when he was informed about Zaynab bint Jahsh, that she prayed the whole night until she tied a rope between two pillars, and when she grew weary she would hold on to it, he disapproved of this and ordered that it be untied.

The seventh is that God praised them, saying that their sides forsake their beds, and they are restless in them until they rise to prayer. For this reason He rewarded them for this forsaking, which was caused by the restlessness and agitation of the heart until it rises to prayer, with a delight for the eyes.

The eighth is that the Companions, who are the first and most entitled to be included in this verse, did not understand from it that they did not sleep at night at all.

Al-Bukhari and others narrated, through Bujayr ibn Saʿd, from Saʿid, from Qatadah, from Anas, concerning God's words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾, that he said: "They used to pray between maghrib and ʿisha."

The ninth is that this interpretation involves disjointing the speech and placing the object of the governing verb before it, because you make (qalilan, "little") the object (maful) of (yahjaʿun, "they sleep"), and the verb is negated. The Basrans do not permit this, though the Kufans do. Some scholars distinguished, permitting it in the case of an adverbial expression (zarf, adverb of time or place) but not in other cases.

(Section)

It has also been said that (ma) is superfluous (zaʾidah), and the predicate of (kana, "they were") is ﴿yahjaʿun﴾, while (qalilan) is in the accusative, either as a verbal noun (masdar), meaning "a little sleeping," or as an adverb of time, meaning "for a little time."

This is objected to on the grounds that sleeping during half the night and standing in prayer during a third, then sleeping during a sixth, is the prayer most beloved to God. So the time of sleep would be greater than the time of prayer, so how would He praise them with what is less excellent?

The answer is that for one who performs this kind of prayer, the time of his sleep is certainly less than the time of his wakefulness. He is awake from maghrib until ʿisha, and from fajr until sunrise. What remains is the period between ʿisha and fajr, and they stand in prayer for half of that period. Thus the time of sleep is less than the time of wakefulness.

It has also been said that (ma) is a verbal noun (masdariyyah), in a position of nominative case following (qalil, "little"). That is, "their sleep was little."

This is the view of al-Hasan (al-Basri).

It has also been said that it is a relative pronoun meaning "that," with the returning pronoun omitted, so the meaning is "a little of the night, the time that they sleep."

But this involves strain (takalluf).

It has also been said that ﴿ma yahjaʿun﴾ is a substitute of inclusion (badal al-ishtimal) for the subject of (kana), and the intended meaning is "their sleeping during the night was little."

This is objected to on the grounds that (min al-layl, "of the night") is connected to (yahjaʿun), and the object of a verbal noun may not precede it.

The answer to this is that the phrase is in the accusative as an explanation (tafsir), meaning that a verb is supposed to be implied for it, to which this mentioned word serves as explanation, and (qalilan) is the predicate of (kana), and the sentence is complete with this.

The meaning is: "They were a group or kind that was few," then He said: ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾.

Those who hold this view take (ma) as negative, so the speech returns to the negation of their sleeping any part of the night, and what is in this has already been mentioned.

Then He informed about them that, along with their prayer at night, they would seek God's forgiveness at the time of dawn (al-sahar). They concluded their prayer with seeking forgiveness and repentance, so they spent the night prostrating and standing for their Lord, then they repented to Him and sought His forgiveness after that.

When the Prophet (ﷺ) finished his prayer, he would seek forgiveness three times.

God commanded him to end his life with seeking forgiveness, and commanded His servants to end their departure from ʿArafat with seeking forgiveness.

It was also prescribed for one performing ablution to end his ablution with repentance. The best things with which deeds can be concluded are repentance and seeking forgiveness.

(Benefit)

Al-Hasan said: "They extended the prayer until dawn (al-sahar), then they sat seeking forgiveness."

(Admonition)

When the night comes on, the battle between sleep and wakefulness begins. Longing and fear form the vanguard of the army of vigilance. Laziness and negligence sit in the battalion of heedlessness. When the seeker charges a sincere charge, he routs the troops of lethargy and sleep. Victory and spoils are achieved, and by the time dawn breaks the shares have been divided, and the sleepers have no news.

Those who rise at night stand on the feet of earnestness beneath the veil of darkness, weeping over a time lost apart from union.

The mounts of wakefulness never cease to traverse the desert of darkness, their eyes of hope seeing nothing but the abode, while the driver of resolve says:

"O company of the night, the journey is pleasant, so seize the traveling by night.
Whoever sleeps the whole night will not arrive."

Until the breeze of dawn blows, and the singer rises seeking the darkness of night. When they are about to depart, the people cling to its hem, weeping over the separation from the Beloved. When dawn breaks, their driver sings. At morning, the people praise the night journey.

O you who regard the states of these people as great, climb the ascending stages, and you will arrive.

[Section: The Fifth of the Corrupters of the Heart: Excessive Sleep]

The fifth corrupter: excessive sleep. It kills the heart, weighs down the body, wastes time, and produces much heedlessness and laziness. Some of it is extremely disliked, and some of it is harmful and does not benefit the body.

The most beneficial sleep is that taken when there is the greatest need for it. Sleep at the beginning of the night is more praiseworthy and more beneficial than sleep at its end. Sleep in the middle of the day is more beneficial than sleep at its beginning or end. The closer sleep is to the two ends, the less its benefit and the greater its harm, especially the sleep of the afternoon, and sleep at the beginning of the day, except for one who stays up at night.

Among what is disliked according to them is sleep between the dawn prayer and sunrise, for it is a time of spoils. Among the wayfarers (al-salikin), using that time for travel has a great merit. Even if they traveled the whole night, they would not allow themselves to sit idle from travel during that time until the sun rises, for it is the beginning of the day and its key, the time when provisions descend, when allotments are received, and when blessing arrives. From it the day arises, and the ruling of the whole day follows the ruling of that portion. Therefore its sleep should be like the sleep of one under compulsion.

In sum, the most balanced and beneficial sleep is sleep during the first half of the night and its last sixth, which amounts to eight hours. This is the most balanced sleep according to physicians, and whatever exceeds it or falls short of it affects the natural temperament in proportion to the deviation.

Among the sleep that also does not benefit is sleep at the beginning of the night, immediately after sunset, before the redness of twilight (fahmat al-ʿisha) disappears. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) disliked it. So it is disliked both by Sharia and by natural constitution.

Just as excessive sleep produces these afflictions, resisting it and abandoning it entirely produces other great afflictions: a bad and dry temperament, deviation of the soul, and the drying up of the moistures that aid understanding and action. It also produces destructive diseases through which the sufferer benefits neither his heart nor his body. Existence is sustained only by balance. Whoever holds fast to it has taken his share of all good. And from God is the help sought.

Among the sleep that also does not benefit is sleep at the beginning of the night, immediately after sunset, before the redness of twilight (fahmat al-ʿisha) disappears. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) disliked it. So it is disliked both by Sharia and by natural constitution.

Just as excessive sleep produces these afflictions, resisting it and abandoning it entirely produces other great afflictions: a bad and dry temperament, deviation of the soul, and the drying up of the moistures that aid understanding and action. It also produces destructive diseases through which the sufferer benefits neither his heart nor his body. Existence is sustained only by balance. Whoever holds fast to it has taken his share of all good. And from God is the help sought.

Then He, glorified is He, informed of their goodness toward creation together with their sincerity toward their Lord, so He combined for them sincerity and goodness, in contrast to ﴿those who make a show of their deeds and withhold simple assistance﴾. He emphasized the sincerity of their goodness by making its recipients the beggar and the deprived, the one for whom they do not intend by their giving any recompense from him or gratitude, and the deprived one who is restrained and does not ask.

Consider the wisdom of the Lord, exalted is He, in that He deprived him by His decree, while He prescribed giving to the possessors of wealth, and He is the Richest of the rich and the most Generous of the generous. Thus He did not combine on him two kinds of deprivation: deprivation by decree and deprivation by law.

He prescribed his giving by His command and deprived him by His decree, so He did not combine on him two deprivations.

(Chapter)

Then He, glorified is He, reminded them of His signs upon the horizons and within themselves, saying: ﴿And in the earth are signs for those who have certainty, and within yourselves. Will you not then see?﴾

The signs of the earth are of many kinds. Among them is its creation and its coming into being after non-existence; and the evidences of its having been brought into existence and of its need for a Creator are upon it, and cannot be denied, for they are established signs within it. Among them is the emergence of this dry part of it above the water, though its natural state would be to be submerged beneath it. Among them is its vastness and the greatness of its creation. Among them is its being spread out, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And at the earth, how it has been spread out?﴾ This does not contradict its being spherical, for in reality it is a sphere which has a surface on which living creatures settle. Among them is that He made it a bed (firash), so that it is the place of rest and dwelling of living beings; He made it a resting-place (qarar), and made it a smooth, submissive cradle (mihad dhalul), trodden by feet, struck by hoes and axes, bearing upon its back heavy buildings. It is submissive, subjugated to whatever the servant wishes from it. He made it a carpet (bisat), and made it a gatherer (kifat) for the living, who it gathers upon its back, and for the dead, whom it gathers into its belly. And (He) "spread it out" (tahaha), that is, stretched it, extended it and made it wide; and (He) "spread it" (dahaha), that is, prepared it for what is intended from it, by bringing forth its water and its pasture, and by splitting rivers within it, and placing in it roads and wide passages. By making it a cradle and a bed, He drew attention to His wisdom in making it still. That is another sign, for there is no support beneath it to hold it, nor any suspension above it; but since it lies upon the surface of the water, it would tilt in it as a ship tilts. Therefore the eternal providence and divine wisdom required that He set upon it firm mountains to fix it, lest it shake, and so that mankind might settle upon it. He made it submissive, with the wisdom that it is not in extreme hardness and rigidity like iron, which would make digging, cleaving, building, planting, sowing, laying down to sleep upon it, and walking on it impossible. By making it a resting-place, He drew attention to the wisdom that it was not created in extreme softness, looseness and smoothness, so that it could not support buildings, nor could living creatures or heavy bodies settle upon it. Rather, He made it between hardness and softness. The noblest substances in the sight of man are gold, silver, ruby and emerald; yet if the earth were made of these substances, the benefits of servants and animals would be lost from it, and the useful purposes intended from it would be nullified. From this it is known that the substances of the dust are nobler than these substances, more beneficial, more blessed, even though those are higher and more precious; their costliness and rarity are due to their scarcity, otherwise dust is more beneficial than them, more blessed and more precious. Likewise, He did not make it transparent, for a transparent body does not retain light, and whatever is like that does not receive heat, so it remains in extreme cold, and living creatures could not settle upon it nor could plants grow in it. Likewise He did not make it polished and shining, lest what is upon it be burnt by the reflection of the sun's rays, as is observed in the burning of cotton and the like when the ray is reflected from a polished, transparent body. Thus the wisdom of God, glorified is He, required that He made it dense and dusty, so that it was fit to be a settling place for animals, mankind and plants.

Since the airborne animal cannot live in water as the aquatic animal does, He manifested its side (of land) as mentioned before, made it in the most suitable forms for its interests, produced from it its food and sustenance, and likewise created the human species from it, returns them to it and brings them forth from it.

(Chapter)

Among its signs is that He made it of differing kinds, qualities and benefits, although they are adjacent, contiguous pieces: here is easy ground, and beside it is rough ground; adjacent to and touching it is fertile land that grows plants, and beside it land that does not grow; here is soil, and touching it is sand; here is hard ground, and adjoining and next to it is soft; here is black, and next to it white earth; here is entirely pebbles, and adjoining it land in which no stone is found; here is suitable for the growth of such-and-such, and here is not suitable for it but for something else; here is salty brackish ground, and here is its opposite; here there is no mountain or landmark, and here it is filled with mountains; here it is suitable only with rain, and here rain does not benefit it, and it is suitable only with irrigation by rivers, so God, glorified is He, sends water as rain upon the distant land, and here rain does not benefit it, so He conveys water to it over the surface of the earth.

So if you were to ask it: who made this variety in its kind? Who divided its parts with this division? Who specified each piece of it with what He specified for it? Who cast upon it its mountains, opened in it its roads, brought forth from it water and pasture? Who holds it from moving? Who blessed in it and decreed in it its sustenance, and produced from it its animals and plants? Who placed in it its minerals, jewels and benefits? Who prepared it as a dwelling and resting place for mankind? Who begins creation from it and then returns it to it, and then brings it forth from it? Who made it submissive, not difficult nor unyielding? Who trod its shoulders, made its paths easy, widened its outlets, split its rivers, caused its trees to grow and brought forth its fruits? Who split it open for plants and deposited in it all sustenance? Who spread it, laid it out as a cradle, made it submissive, spread it and extended it, and made what is upon it an adornment for it? And who holds it from shaking, so that it trembles and whatever buildings and landmarks are upon it fall, or who causes it to swallow those upon it, so that it then quakes? Who produced from it the human species, which is the most wondrous of creatures and the finest of made things? Indeed, He produced from it Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus and Muhammad, upon them all be peace; and He produced from it His friends, beloved ones and righteous servants. Who made it a keeper of what has been entrusted to it of waters, provisions, minerals and animals? Who placed between it and the sun and moon this measure of distance? For if it were more than this, its receiving of the sun's heat and the moon's light would weaken, and the benefit reaching animals and plants by that would be lost; and if it were nearer, the heat and warmth would intensify, as we observe in summer, and the bodies of animals and plants would be burnt. In sum, this wisdom by which the world is ordered would be lost. Who placed in it gardens, orchards and springs? Who made its inside houses for the dead and its outside houses for the living? Who gives it life after its death, sending down water upon it from the sky, then sending the wind upon it, and the sun rising over it, so that it begins to swell? When the time of birth comes, it is stirred for delivery, shakes, and brings forth every lovely pair.

Glorified is He who made the sky like the father and the earth like the mother, and the rain like the water from which the child is conceived. When the seed is placed in the earth and water falls upon it, the moisture of the mud acts upon it, and the hidden warmth within the earth assists it, so that the moisture and heat reach the inside of the seed; the seed expands, grows and swells, and splits into two shoots: one shoot above, which is the tree, and one shoot below, which is the root. Then that offspring grows until his father has no relation to him left. Then after his father, he produces thousands upon thousands of offspring. All this is the work of the Wise Lord in a single seed, which may reach great size from a small beginning. This is from the blessing that God, glorified is He, placed in this mother. How wondrous a sign, sufficient by itself to demonstrate the existence of the Creator, His attributes of perfection and His actions, and the truthfulness of His messengers in what they reported of Him, namely the bringing forth of those in the graves for the Day of Resurrection and Gathering.

Reflect upon the gathering of these four elements, their adjacency, their mixing, the need of some of them for others, the separation of some from others, and the effect of each upon the other, and the effect of the other upon it, such that it can do nothing but follow in being affected and acted upon; neither one independently exerts influence, nor is one free of the other. In this is the clearest proof that they are created, made, sustained, managed, and originated after non-existence, needy of a Originator who is independent of them, an Agent not acted upon, eternal and not originated; all created things submit to His power, answer the call of His will, respond to the call of His oneness and lordship, testify to His knowledge and wisdom, call His servants to remember Him, thank Him, obey Him, serve Him and love Him, warn them of His might and vengeance, and urge them to hasten toward His good pleasure and Paradise.

Look at water and earth: how, when the Lord, exalted is He, willed their mixing and pairing, He produced winds which stirred the water and drove it until they cast it into the depths of the earth; then He produced for it a subtle heavenly warmth, by which growth occurred; then He produced for it another, stronger heat, by which splitting open took place. Its first state was too weak for the second heat, so it was stored until the time of its strength and firmness. Thus the spring warmth is for bringing forth, and the summer warmth is for ripening. Yet the mother is one, the father is one, the fertilization is one, and the offspring are of extreme diversity and variety, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And in the earth are neighbouring tracts, and gardens of vines, and crops and palm trees, growing from one root or not, watered with one water; yet We make some of them excel others in fruit. Indeed in that are signs for a people who use reason.﴾

This is some of the signs of the earth. Among the signs in it are His acts which He inflicted upon the peoples who denied their messengers and opposed His command, and He left their traces as evidence of them, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And 'Ad and Thamud—and it has become clear to you from their dwellings.﴾ And He said concerning the people of Lot: ﴿And indeed you pass by them in the morning, and at night. Will you not then reason?﴾

And He said: ﴿So the Cry seized them at sunrise; then We turned it upside down and rained upon them stones of baked clay. Indeed in that are signs for those who discern. And indeed it is on a road that remains.﴾ That is, on a firm path that does not pass from its condition.

And He said: ﴿And indeed the companions of the Thicket were wrongdoers; so We took vengeance upon them, and indeed the two are on a clear highway.﴾ That is, the abodes of these two peoples are on a clear road that travellers pass by.

And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it became clear to you how We dealt with them.﴾

And He said concerning the people of 'Ad: ﴿So they became such that nothing could be seen except their dwellings.﴾

And He said: ﴿Has it not guided them how many generations We destroyed before them, through whose dwellings they walk?﴾ So what greater proof is there than a man who goes out alone, with no supporters, no number, and no wealth, calling a mighty nation to the oneness of God, faith in Him and obedience to Him, and warning them of His might and vengeance; then their word, or most of them, agrees upon denying him and opposing him, so He reminds them of kinds of punishment beyond human power: He drowns all the deniers at one time, sinks others into the earth at another, destroys others with wind, others with the Cry, others by transformation, others with thunderbolts, and others with various punishments; while their caller and those with him are saved, and those destroyed are many times over in number, strength, might and wealth.

﻿﻿So how wondrous are the signs of truth, if the seeker of truth were to be guided by them, becoming a guide!
But upon those hearts are coverings; though they listen, they do not answer the caller.

Why then did they not refrain, if they were upon the truth, while they were the more numerous and more powerful in strength, from His might and authority? Why did they not take refuge from His punishment, as those weaker than them among the followers of the messengers took refuge?

Among the signs in the earth is what God produces in it at all times, which confirms what His messengers reported. The signs of the messengers, the marks of their truthfulness and the proofs of their prophethood, are continually produced by God, exalted is He, in the earth as a establishment of proof against those who did not witness those signs, signs which were close to the age of the messengers; so much so that the people of each century seem to witness what the earlier ones witnessed, or its equivalent, as He said: ﴿We shall show them Our signs upon the horizons and within themselves, until it becomes clear to them that it is the Truth.﴾

This will is not restricted to one century rather than another; rather, God, glorified is He, must show the people of every century signs which make clear to them that He is God, there is no god but Him, and that His messengers are truthful. The signs of the earth are greater than what has been mentioned and more numerous; He alerted us to the abundant by means of the little among them.

[Section: The Station of Certainty]

Among the stations of "You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help" is the station of certainty (yaqin).

It stands to faith as the spirit stands to the body. By it the knowers excel, through it the competitors compete, toward it the workers strive, the deeds of the people are upon it, and all their allusions point to it. When patience is wed to certainty, there is born between them the attainment of leadership in religion. God, the Exalted, said, and by His word the rightly guided are guided: ﴿And We made from among them leaders guiding by Our command, when they were patient and certain of Our signs.﴾ [al-Sajdah: 24]

God, glorified is He, singled out the people of certainty for benefiting from the signs and proofs. He said, and He is the most truthful of speakers: ﴿And in the earth are signs for the certain.﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 20]

He singled out the people of certainty for guidance and success among all the worlds, saying: ﴿And those who believe in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you, and in the Hereafter they are certain. Those are upon guidance from their Lord, and those are the successful.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 4-5]

He informed about the people of the Fire that they were not among the people of certainty, saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when it was said, "Indeed the promise of God is true, and the Hour, there is no doubt about it," you said, "We do not know what the Hour is; we only assume an assumption, and we are not certain."﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 32]

So certainty is the spirit of the deeds of the heart, which are the spirits of the deeds of the limbs.

It is the reality of truthfulness (siddiqiyyah), and it is the pivot of this affair upon which its axis turns.

Khalid ibn Yazid related from al-Sufyanayn, from al-Taymi, from Khaythamah, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Do not please anyone by the displeasure of God; do not praise anyone for the favour of God; and do not blame anyone for what God has not given you. For the provision of God is not driven to you by the greed of a greedy person, nor is it turned away from you by the aversion of one who dislikes it. Indeed God, in His justice and equity, placed comfort and joy in contentment and certainty, and placed worry and grief in doubt and displeasure."

Certainty is the companion of trust in God (tawakkul). For this reason tawakkul has been explained as the strength of certainty.

The correct view is that trust is its fruit and result. For this reason the combination of guidance with it is fitting. God said: ﴿So put your trust in God; indeed you are upon the manifest truth.﴾ [al-Naml: 79]

So the truth is certainty. And the messengers of God said: ﴿And why should we not put our trust in God, when He has guided us to our ways?﴾ [Ibrahim: 12]

When certainty reaches the heart, the heart becomes filled with light and radiance, and every doubt, suspicion, displeasure, anxiety and grief is removed from it. It becomes filled with love for God, fear of Him, contentment with Him, gratitude to Him, trust in Him, and turning back to Him in repentance. It is thus the material of all the stations and the carrier of them.

It has been disputed whether it is acquired or bestowed. It was said: it is the knowledge deposited in hearts, pointing to its not being acquired.

Sahl said: certainty is from the increase of faith, and there is no doubt that faith is acquired.

The verified view is that it is acquired in terms of its causes, and bestowed in terms of its own essence and reality.

Sahl said: its beginning is unveiling (mukashafah), as one of the early scholars said: "If the veil were lifted, I would not increase in certainty." Then comes direct witnessing (mu'ayanah) and observation (mushahadah).

Ibn Khafif said: it is the realization of secrets through judgments about unseen matters.

Abu Bakr ibn Zahir said: knowledge may be opposed by doubts, but certainty has no doubt in it.

Among the people (of Sufism): certainty does not dwell in a heart in which there is repose in anything other than God.

Dhu al-Nun said: certainty calls to shortening hope, shortening hope calls to asceticism, and asceticism produces wisdom, and wisdom produces reflection upon consequences.

He said: Three are the markers of certainty (aʿlām al-yaqīn): little mixing with people in companionship; leaving off praising them for giving; and keeping oneself free of blaming them when refusing. And three of its markers as well: looking to God in everything; returning to Him in every matter; and seeking His help in every state.

Al-Junayd said: Certainty (al-yaqīn) is the settling of knowledge that does not turn over, is not transformed, and does not change in the heart.

Ibn ʿAṭāʾ said: According to their closeness to piety (al-taqwā) they attain of certainty.

The root of piety is separation from what is forbidden, and that is separation from the self (al-nafs). So according to their departure from the self, they reach certainty.

It was said: Certainty is unveiling (al-mukāshafa). It has three aspects: unveiling in reports; unveiling through the manifestation of power; and the unveiling of hearts to the realities of faith.

The people's meaning by unveiling is that a thing becomes manifest to the heart in such a way that its relation to it is like the relation of the seen to the eye.

So no doubt and no uncertainty remain with you at all. This is the ultimate of faith, and it is the station of excellence (iḥsān).

They may also mean by it another matter: what one of them sees in an intermediate state between sleep and wakefulness at the first stages of the soul's detachment from the body.

Whoever among them points to other than these two has erred and been confused.

Al-Sarrī said: Certainty is your stillness when the thoughts (al-mawārid) roam in your breast, because you are certain that your movement in them does not benefit you, and does not turn away from you what has been decreed.

Abū Bakr al-Warrāq said: Certainty is the mainstay of the heart, through it comes the perfection of faith, and through certainty God is known; by reason, one understands from God.

Al-Junayd said: Men have walked on water by certainty, and one better than them in certainty has died of thirst.

There has been disagreement over whether certainty is superior to presence (al-ḥuḍūr), or presence superior to certainty.

It was said: presence is superior, because it is settling (waṭanāt), while certainty is passing thoughts (khaṭarāt). Some preferred certainty and said: it is the goal of faith. The first view saw that certainty is the beginning of presence, as if he made certainty the start and presence the constant state.

This disagreement is not clear, for certainty is never separated from presence, nor presence from certainty. Rather, in certainty there is an increase of faith, knowledge of its details and branches, and placing them in their proper stations, which is not in presence. So it is more complete than presence in this respect. And in presence there is gathering (al-jamʿiyya), non-separation, and entering into annihilation (al-fanāʾ), which certainty may be separated from. So certainty is more specific to knowledge, and presence is more specific to will. And God knows best.

Al-Nahrajūrī said: When the servant completes the realities of certainty, affliction becomes for him a blessing, and ease becomes for him a calamity.

Abū Bakr al-Warrāq said: Certainty is of three aspects: certainty of report (yaqīn khabar), certainty of indication (yaqīn dalāla), and certainty of witnessing (yaqīn mushāhada).

By certainty of report he means the heart's rest in the report of the reporter and its trust in him. By certainty of indication he means what is above it, which is that he establishes for him, together with his confidence in his truthfulness, the proofs indicating what he reported.

This is like the general reports of faith, tawḥīd, and the Qur'an. For He, glorified is He, despite being the most truthful of the truthful, establishes for His servants proofs, parables, and demonstrations of the truthfulness of His reports. So certainty is attained for them from both aspects: from the side of the report and from the side of the proof.

Thus they rise from that to the third level, which is the certainty of unveiling, such that what is reported becomes for their hearts like the seen for their eyes. Then the relation of faith in the Unseen to the heart is like the relation of the seen to the eye. This is the highest kind of unveiling, and it is what ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Qays indicated in his saying: "Had the veil been lifted, I would not have increased in certainty." This is not from the speech of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), nor from the saying of ʿAlī, as one who has no knowledge of transmitted reports might suppose.

Some of them said: I saw Paradise and Hell in reality. It was said to him: How? He said: I saw them with the eyes of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and my seeing them with his eyes is more precious to me than my seeing them with my own eyes, for my sight may transgress and swerve, unlike his sight (ﷺ).

Certainty drives its possessor toward terrors and the riding of dangers; it always commands advancement. If knowledge does not accompany it, it carries its possessor into ruin.

Knowledge commands delay and holding back. If certainty does not accompany it, it keeps its companion from gains and spoils. And God knows best.

[Degrees of Certainty]

[The First Degree: ʿIlm al-Yaqīn (Knowledge of Certainty)]

It has three degrees.

The first degree: knowledge of certainty. It is accepting what has appeared of the Truth, accepting what is hidden for the Truth, and standing upon what has been established by the Truth.

The Shaykh mentioned in this degree three things, which are the object of certainty and its pillars.

The first: accepting what has appeared of the Truth, may He be exalted. What has appeared from Him, glorified is He, is His commands, His prohibitions, His law, and His religion, which has become manifest to us through the tongues of His messengers. So we receive it with acceptance, submission, surrender, and yielding to Lordship, and entry under the bondage of servanthood.

The second: accepting what is hidden for the Truth, which is faith in the Unseen that the Truth, glorified is He, reported through His messengers concerning the matters of the Return and its details: Paradise and Hell, and what precedes that: the Bridge, the Balance, and the Reckoning, and what precedes that: the splitting and cleaving of the heaven, the scattering of the stars, the blowing away of the mountains, and the folding up of the world; and what precedes that: the matters of the barzakh, its bliss and its punishment.

So accepting all of this, with faith, affirmation, and certainty, is certainty, such that no doubt, no suspicion, no forgetfulness, and no heedlessness enters the heart concerning it. For if one's certainty does not perish, it corrupts and weakens it.

The third: standing upon what has been established by the Truth, glorified is He, of His names, attributes, and actions.

This is the knowledge of tawḥīd, whose foundation is affirming the names and attributes. Its opposite is ta'ṭīl (negation) and denial, and extremism. This tawḥīd is opposed by ta'ṭīl.

As for intentional, volitional tawḥīd, which is sincerity of action for God and worshipping Him alone, it is opposed by shirk. Ta'ṭīl is worse than shirk, for the one who denies (muʿaṭṭil) rejects the Essence or its perfection, and that is a denial of the reality of divinity.

For a being that does not hear, does not see, does not speak, does not approve, does not become angry, and does not act, and is neither within the world nor outside it, neither connected to the world nor separated from it, neither distant from it nor opposed to it, neither adjacent nor transcending, neither above the Throne nor below the Throne, neither behind it nor in front of it, neither to its right nor to its left, is the same as non-existence.

The polytheist affirms God and His attributes, but he worshipped another with Him. So he is better than the one who denies the Essence and the attributes.

Thus certainty is standing upon what has been established by the Truth of His names, attributes, the descriptions of His perfection, and His tawḥīd. These three are the most noble of the knowledge of creation: the knowledge of command and prohibition, the knowledge of names, attributes, and tawḥīd, and the knowledge of the Return and the Last Day. And God knows best.

[Section: The Second Degree, ʿAyn al-Yaqīn (Eye of Certainty)]

He said: The second degree: eye of certainty. It is one who, through the seeing, needs no inference, and through direct observation needs no report, and whose witnessing tears through the veil of knowledge.

The difference between knowledge of certainty and eye of certainty is like the difference between a true report and direct sight. The truth of certainty is above this.

I have illustrated the three levels with one who tells you that he has honey, and you do not doubt his truthfulness. Then he shows it to you, and you gain more certainty. Then you taste it.

The first is knowledge of certainty; the second is eye of certainty; the third is truth of certainty.

So our knowledge now of Paradise and Hell is knowledge of certainty. When Paradise is brought near for the righteous at the place of standing, and creation witnesses it, and Hellfire is made manifest for the deviators, and creation sees it with their own eyes, that is eye of certainty. When the people of Paradise are admitted to Paradise and the people of the Fire to the Fire, that then is truth of certainty.

His saying: "It is one who, through the seeing, needs no inference."

By inference he means perception and witnessing. That is, its possessor has become independent of seeking proof, for one only seeks proof so that knowledge of the thing proven may be attained. When the thing proven is witnessed by him, and he has perceived it by his unveiling, what need has he for inference?

This is the meaning of being independent of report through direct observation.

As for his saying: "and whose witnessing tears through the veil of knowledge."

He means: the cognitions that come to the possessor of this degree are from witnessing that tears through the veil of knowledge. For knowledge is a veil from witnessing. So in this degree the veil is lifted and it leads to the known, such that it confronts his insight and his heart in direct confrontation.

[Section: The Third Degree, Ḥaqq al-Yaqīn (Truth of Certainty)]

He said: The third degree: truth of certainty. It is the brightening of the dawn of unveiling, then deliverance from the burden of certainty, then annihilation in the truth of certainty.

Know that this degree is not attained in this world except by the messengers, may God's blessings and peace be upon them all. For our Prophet (ﷺ) saw Paradise and Hell with his eye, and Moses (peace be upon him) heard the speech of God from Him to him without intermediary, and God spoke to him directly. And He manifested Himself to the mountain while Moses was looking, and He made it crumble to dust.

Yes, truth of certainty is attained for us from one station, which is tasting what the Messenger (ﷺ) reported of the realities of faith connected with the hearts and their deeds. For when the heart engages with them and tastes them, they become for it truth of certainty.

As for the matters of the Hereafter and the Return, and seeing God openly with the eye, and hearing His speech in reality without intermediary, the believer's portion of it in this abode is faith and knowledge of certainty. Truth of certainty is postponed until the time of meeting.

But since the wayfarer in his view reaches annihilation, realizes the witnessing of the Reality, and arrives at the unity of gathering, he said: truth of certainty is the brightening of the dawn of unveiling.

He means: its realization and establishment, and the overcoming of its light over the darkness of the night of the veil. So he moves from the stage of knowledge to being immersed in witnessing, by annihilation from the outward form entirely.

His saying: "then deliverance from the burden of certainty."

He means: certainty has rights that its possessor must discharge, and he must uphold them and bear their burdens and hardships. When he is annihilated in tawḥīd, other very lofty and elevated matters come to him, in which he becomes carried rather than carrying, and flying rather than walking, so the burden of bearing those rights is removed from him. Rather, it remains for him like breath, and like water for the fish.

This is a matter whose judgment is by taste and perception, so do not hasten to deny it.

((Part Seventeen)) Consider the state of that Companion who had dates, sitting eating them, in need of them and hungry and in want of them. When he saw the marketplace of martyrdom rising, he threw his provision from his hand and said: "It would be a long life, if I remained until I eat these dates." He threw them from his hand, fought until he was killed. Likewise were the states of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, matching what he indicated.

But a great point remains, which is the place of prostration: their annihilation was not in the tawḥīd of Lordship and the witnessing of the Reality that the people of annihilation point to, but in the tawḥīd of divinity (al-ilāhiyya). So they annihilated through love of Him, exalted is He, from love of anything else, and through His desire for them from their own desires and portions. So they were not acting out of annihilation, nor absorption in witnessing, such that they annihilate through it from the desire of their Beloved for them; rather they have annihilated in His will from their own will.
