So they are a people of subsistence within annihilation, of distinction within gathering, of multiplicity within unity, and of cosmic reality within religious reality.

They are the people; there is no people but them, and had it not been for them we would not have been guided to the way. So the correct and complete relation of the states of those who came after them to their states is like the relation of what seeps from a vessel to what is within it.

As for deviant and corrupt paths, they are a way other than their way. And grace is in God's hand; He gives it to whom He wills. And God is the Possessor of great grace.

(Note)
Man is a proof in himself of the existence of his Creator, of His oneness, of the truthfulness of His messengers, and of the affirmation of His attributes of perfection.

He (Ibn al-Qayyim) said in (al-Madarij):

All existing things together are witnesses to the attributes, qualities and names of the Lord, majestic is His majesty. They all point to the Most Beautiful Names and their realities, call out to them, indicate them, and inform of them, by the tongue of speech and of state, as it has been said:

Reflect upon the lines of created beings, for they
Are messages to you from the Most High King.

And He has inscribed in them, if you reflect upon their inscription,
Know that everything other than God is vain.

They point to the affirmation of attributes for their Lord,
So the silent among them guides, as does the one who speaks.

You do not see anything that indicates something more clearly than the indication of created beings to the attributes of their Creator, the qualities of His perfection, and the realities of His names. Their indications vary according to their variety: they indicate by reason and by the senses, by innate nature, by reflection, and by contemplation.

(Section)

Then he said: ﴿And within yourselves. Will you not then see?﴾

Since the closest of things to man is himself, his Creator, Shaper, Fashioner and Originator calls him, from a drop of water, to observe and reflect upon himself. When a person reflects upon himself, the signs of lordship shine forth for him, the lights of certainty blaze for him, and the darkness of doubt and suspicion dissipates from him, and the veils of ignorance are lifted from him. For when he looks into himself, he finds the traces of governance standing within him, and the proofs of the oneness of his Lord speaking, bearing witness to his Governor, indicating Him and guiding to Him. He finds himself formed from a drop of water, into fleshy masses arranged, bones assembled, joints multiple and bound firmly with the cords of veins and nerves, wrapped and tightened and gathered within a strong skin, containing three hundred and sixty joints, between large and small, thick and thin, elongated and round, straight and curved. These joints are fastened with three hundred and sixty veins, for connection and separation, grasping and spreading, extension and contraction, and for crafts and writing.

He placed in him nine openings: two openings for hearing, two for sight, two for smell, two for speech, food, drink and breath, and two for the expulsion of waste whose retention would harm him. Inside the two hearing openings He placed something bitter and deadly, lest an insect enter and reach the brain and harm it. Inside the two sight openings He placed something salty, lest constant heat melt the fat there. Inside the opening of food and drink He placed something sweet, so that it makes what he eats and drinks palatable, so that he is not distressed by it, as it would be if it were bitter or salty.

He placed in him two lamps of light, like a shining lantern, set in the highest place of him and in the most noble of his organs, as a vanguard for him. He set this light in a very small part by which he sees the sky, the earth and what is between them. He covered it with seven layers and three humours, one above another, as protection, safeguarding and guarding. Over its place He set a closure with two leaves, upper and lower, and in the edges of the two leaves He set eyelashes of hair, as protection for the eye and as adornment and beauty. Above all of this He set two eyebrows of hair, which shield the eye from falling sweat and catch what drips down from there. Glorified is He, He assigned to each layer of the eye a specific function, and to each humour a specific measure. Were anything added to that or taken from it, the required benefits and interests would be disrupted.

He made this seeing light the size of a lens, then displayed in that lens the image of the sky, the earth, the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, and the upper and lower worlds, with the breadth of their extremities and the distance of their regions. His wisdom, glorified is He, required that He place in it whiteness and blackness. He placed the power of sight in the blackness, and made the whiteness its resting place and dwelling, and adorned each with the other. He made the pupil protected by the eyelids and eyebrows, as mentioned, and the eyebrows by the eyelashes. He made it black, for if it were white, the seeing light would scatter and perception would weaken; blackness gathers the sight and prevents the seeing light from dispersing. For moving and turning the pupil, glorified is He, He created twenty-four muscles; if a single muscle were lacking, the matter of the eye would be disrupted.

Since the eye is like a mirror, in which images are imprinted only when it is in the utmost polish and clarity, He, glorified is He, made these eyelids naturally very quick to close, without effort, so that this mirror remains pure and clear from all impurities. For this reason, the fly, which has no eyelids, is constantly seen cleaning its eye with its hand from traces of dust and impurities.

(Section)

Just as He, glorified is He, made the two eyes conveyors to the heart of what they see, so that they deliver it to it as you see, He made them mirrors of the heart, in which there appears what is deposited within it of love and hatred, good and evil, dullness and sharpness, deviation and uprightness. One thus deduces the states of the heart from the states of the eye. This is one of the three kinds of physiognomy: the physiognomy of the eye, the physiognomy of the ear, and the physiognomy of the heart. The eye is a mirror of the heart, a vanguard, a messenger. Among the wonders of it is that it is among the most delicate of organs and the least affected by heat and cold, although the ear, despite its hardness and thickness, is affected by them more than the eye despite its delicacy. This is not due to the covering of eyelids over it, for if it were open it would not be affected by that as delicate organs are.

(Section)

Among that: the two ears, which He, blessed and exalted, split in the two sides of the face, and in which He deposited moisture that aids the perception of hearing, and deposited within them the power of hearing. Glorified is He, He placed in this passage ? turns and windings, to lengthen the distance slightly, so that air reaches only after its force has been broken, so that it does not strike it in one blow and harm it. Also, lest the entering creeping things and insects surprise it; rather, if something enters one of those bends, it stops there and is easily removed.

The eyes were placed in the middle of the face and the ears on its sides, because the eyes are the seat of beauty, adornment and loveliness, and are like the light that walks before a person. As for the ears, they were placed on the sides because their perception of what is behind and in front of a person, to his right and to his left, is equal, so that sounds reach them in one proportion. The eyes were made with a covering and the ears without one. This is in the utmost wisdom, for if the ears had a covering, it would prevent the perception of sound, which would occur only after the covering was lifted; and sound is an accident with no permanence, so it would vanish before the covering was removed. This is unlike what is seen by the eye, for those are bodies and accidents that do not vanish between the lifting of the covering and the opening of the eye. Glorified is He, He made the ear a cartilaginous organ, neither loose flesh nor hard bone, but between hardness and softness: it receives by its softness and retains by its hardness, does not split as bones split, and is not affected by heat, cold, sun and hot wind as flesh is affected, since the benefit lies in its projection, to receive the sounds and reports that reach it.

(Section)

Among that: the nose, which He, glorified is He, set in the middle of the face, upright and balanced, in the finest shape and most suited to benefit, and in which He deposited the sense of smell, by which it perceives scents, their kinds, qualities, benefits and harms, and by which one deduces the harms and benefits of foods and medicines. Also, by inhaling through it, it draws in cool, moist air and carries it to the heart, so that the heart is refreshed by it, and so one never needs to open the mouth. He made its cavity as large as needed: He did not widen it so that much air would enter, nor narrow it so that insufficient air would enter. He made that cavity elongated so that the air is contained within it and its cold and heat are broken before it reaches the brain; otherwise it would strike the brain with its heat and force.

The air that the nose inhales divides into two parts: one part ascends to the brain, and one part descends to the lung. It is also one of the instruments of speech, for it aids in articulating the letters. Just as its cavity was made for inhaling air, it was made as an outlet for the brain's waste, which flows down through that passage and exits, so the brain is relieved. For this reason He placed a covering over it and did not make it protruding, lest the eyes find it ugly. He placed in it two cavities, for one of them may become blocked or suffer an ailment that prevents perception and inhalation, and then the second cavity remains as its deputy, performing its function, as wisdom requires, as with the two eyes.

Then consider the air that the nose inhales: how it first enters through the nostrils, and its coldness is broken there; then it reaches the throat, where its temperament is balanced; then it reaches the lung in its finest state; then the lung sends it to the heart, which is refreshed from the innate heat within it; then it passes from the heart into the moving veins and reaches the farthest extremities of the body. Then, when it has been heated within and has left the limit of benefit, it leaves those extremities back into the body, then to the lung, then to the windpipe, then to the nostrils, going out through them, and in its place returns cool, beneficial air. A single breath of the servant's breaths is completed only by the totality of these matters, powers and actions. He has, in a day and a night, twenty-four thousand breaths, and for God there are in each breath numerous blessings, of which I have comprehended only a few. So what do you think of what lies beyond breathing, of the organs and powers and their benefits, and the completion of blessing through them?!

(Section)

As for the mouth, it is the place of wonders, the gate of food, drink, breath and speech, and the dwelling of the speaking tongue, which is the instrument of knowledge, the interpreter of the heart and its messenger who conveys its message.

Since the heart is the king of the body and the source of innate heat, when cool air enters it reaches the heart, its temperature is balanced, and it remains there a while; then it warms up and is burned, so the heart needs to expel and remove it. The Wisest of the wise made its expulsion the cause of the arising of sound in the larynx, the palate, the tongue, the lips and the teeth, which are articulation points and various exits. By their differing, the letters are distinguished from one another. Then He inspired the servant to combine those letters, to convey through them what the heart commands.

Consider the dazzling wisdom: He, glorified is He, did not make that expelled breath, which the body has no need of and must push out, merely waste; rather, when it is no longer needed, He placed in it a benefit and an interest that are among the most perfect benefits and interests. For the primary purpose of breath is the cool air's reaching the heart; as for exhaling, it is like expelling a corrupt waste. Glorified is He, He redirected it to the care of another interest and benefit, and made it the cause of sounds, letters and speech.

Then He, glorified is He, made the throats of different shapes in narrowness and width, roughness and smoothness, so that sounds differ by their difference, and no two sounds resemble each other, just as no two forms resemble each other. This is among the clearest proofs: this variation among forms and sounds, despite their multiplicity and number, rarely makes two sounds or two forms alike, and nature does not require this; it is only the handiwork of God, who perfected everything and made beautifully everything He created. Blessed is God, Lord of the worlds, and the best of creators. Thus, glorified is He, He distinguished between persons by what hearing and sight perceive.

(Section)

He placed in the tongue, among its benefits, the benefit of speech, which is the greatest of them, and the benefit of taste and perception. He made it an indicator of the balance or imbalance of the heart's temperament, just as He made it an indicator of its uprightness or crookedness. Thus the physician deduces from what appears on the tongue of roughness, smoothness, whiteness, redness, cracking and other features the state of the heart and temperament; and it is a strong indicator of the states of the stomach and intestines. Just as the listener deduces from what appears in a person's speech what is in his heart, so the soundness or corruption of the heart appears in it, in meaning and in form.

(Section)

Glorified is He, He made the tongue a fleshy organ with no bone or sinew in it, so that its movement is easy. For this reason you will not find among the organs any that does not tire from frequent movement except it; for any other organ, if you moved it as the tongue moves, could not bear it, and would soon tire and settle into stillness. Also, it is among the most balanced and most delicate of organs, and within the organs it holds the position of the king's messenger and deputy. Its temperament is among the most balanced temperaments of the body, and it needs gripping, extending and movement in the far reaches and sides of the mouth. Had it contained bones, this would not have been possible, nor would complete speech or complete taste. He made it so, as the efficient and final causes required, and God knows best.

(Section)

Glorified is He, He placed two locks on the tongue: one is the teeth, and the second is the mouth. He made its movement voluntary. He placed one covering over the eye and no covering over the ear. This is because of the tongue's importance and nobility, the significance of its movements, and its position in the mouth like the heart in the chest. This is one of the subtleties: the harms of speech are more numerous than the harms of sight, and the harms of sight are more numerous than the harms of hearing. So He gave the organ with the most harms two layers of protection, the intermediate one a single layer, and the one with the fewest harms no layer at all.

(Section)

Glorified is He, He made the mouth the most moist of the organs, and saliva is constantly secreted into it and never leaves it. He made it sweet, neither salty like the water of the eye, nor bitter like what is in the ear, nor foul like what is in the nose; rather it is the sweetest and most pleasant of the body's waters, by profound wisdom. For food and drink mix with it; indeed it is what transforms food and mixes with it as dough mixes with water. Were it not sweet, a person would not enjoy food or drink, nor would any animal, and he would swallow it only with distaste and distress. Since much food cannot be transformed except after being cooked, the Lord, exalted is He, gave it an instrument for cutting and dividing and an instrument for grinding. He made the instrument of cutting, namely the incisors and what is next to them, sharp-edged so that cutting is easy; and He made the molars and what is next to them, with flat, broad crowns, so that grinding is possible. He arranged them in the finest order, like pearls strung on a thread. He placed them on the upper and lower sides so that cutting and grinding can be accomplished, and on the right and left sides, for perhaps one of the two instruments may become blunt, or be disabled, or suffer some accident, and then one turns to the other instrument. Also, were the work always on one side, it would be likely to become disabled or weakened.

Consider how He, glorified is He, caused them to grow from the flesh of the gums, emerging through them as seed grows in the earth. He did not clothe them with flesh as He clothed the other bones, for had flesh covered them, the intended benefit would have been lost. Since bones need flesh to cover and protect them, and to receive heat and cold and to keep their moisture, the interest of the animal would not be complete without this covering; yet since the human bones in one respect need it and in another respect do without it, their covering was made separate from them, and they themselves were made bare, so that the benefit is complete. And since the instruments of cutting, breaking and grinding did not grow with the child from the very beginning of his life like his other bones, for he had no need of them, they were withheld during the time he was independent of them through suckling, and given when he needed them.

In it is another wisdom: had they grown with him from the moment of birth, they would have harmed the nipple, for he has no intellect to guard against biting it, and the mother would have refrained from nursing him.

Among its wonders is the agreement and cooperation between it and the stomach. It hands over to it hard, dry things, and it grinds them, then hands them over to the tongue, which moves them, then the tongue hands them to the throat, which conveys them to the stomach, which ripens and cooks them, then sends from it what is assigned to each. If the teeth are unable to cut and grind something, the stomach is unable to ripen and cook it; if the teeth grow weary, the stomach grows weary; if they weaken, it weakens.

It accompanies a person and serves him, unseen by him; but when his eye falls upon it, it leaves him forever. It is a weapon, a saw, a knife, a spirit, and an adornment, and it has benefits and interests beyond these.

(Section)

ثم تأمل حال الشعر ومنبته وسببه فإن البدن لما كان حارًا رطبًا والحرارة إذا عملت في الرطوبة فلا بد أن تثير بخارًا وتلك الأبخرة تتصاعد من عمق البدن إلى سطحه وتريد الانفصال من هناك فلا بد أن تحدث مساما ومنافذ في ظاهر الجلد وتلك الأبخرة إما أن تكون رطبة لطيفة فحينئذ تنفصل من المسام ولا تحدث شيئًا وإما أن تكون دخانية يابسة غليظة فالجلد حينئذ إما أن يكون في نهاية النعومة والنضارة كجلد الصبيان أو في غاية اليبس والقشف أو يكون معتدلًا فإذ ذاك لا يتولد فيه الشعر لأن البخار إذا شق سطح الجلد وانفصل عاد الجلد في الحال إلى اتصاله الأول بسبب كثرة رطوبته ونعومته مثاله السمك إذا رفع رأسه من الماء إنشق له الماء فإذا عاد إلى الماء عاد الماء إلى اتصاله الأول وكذلك نشاهد الأشياء الرطبة كالنشاء مثلًا إذا أغلي فخرج البخار من موضع الغليان عادت الرطوبة إلى الموضع الذي خرج منه ذلك البخار فسدته فإن كان الجلد في غاية اليبس لم يتولد الشعر لأن الجلد اليابس إذا انثقب بقيت تلك الثقب مفتوحة ليبس الجلد فيفرق أجزاءه البخار ولا يجتمع بعضه إلى بعض فإن الجلد متوسط بين النعومة والكثافة فإنه ينفتح فيه المسام بسبب تلك الأبخرة ولا يعود ينسد بعد خروج البخار ولكن لا تبقى المسام شديدة الانفتاح وحينئذ يبقى ذلك البخار الدخاني في تلك الثقبة لا يزال يمده بخار آخر يدفعه أولًا فأولًا إلى خارج من غير أن ينقطع أصله فيبقى بعضه مركوزًا في الجلد منزلته منزلة أصل النبات وبعضه يطلع إلى خارج منزلته منزلة ساق النبات وكذلك الشعر فمادة الشعر هي البخار الدخاني اليابس وسببه هو الحرارة الطبيعية المحرقة لذلك البخار والآلة التي بها يتم أمره هي المسام التي ارتكن فيها البخار فتلبد هناك فصار شعرًا بإذن الله تعالى.

والغاية التي من أجلها وجد شيئان أحدهما عام وهو تنقية البدن من الفضول الدخانية الغليظة والآخر خاص وهو إما للزينة وإما للوقاية.

وإذا بان أن الشعر إنما يتولد مع الحرارة واليبس المعتدل بقيت ثلاثة أقسام أحدها حرارة غالبة على اليبس كالصبيان الثاني عكسه وهو يبس غالب على الحرارة كالمشائخ الثالث حرارة ضعيفة ويبس ضعيف كأبدان النساء ففي هذه الأقسام يقل الشعر وأما الشباب فإن حرارة أبدانهم ويبسهم معتدل فيقوى تولد الشعر فيهم.

وفي شعر الرأس منافع ومصالح منها وقايته عن الحر والبرد والمرض ومنها الزينة والحسن.

والسبب الذي صار به شعر الرأس أكثر من شعر البدن هو أن البخار شأنه أن يصعد من جميع البدن إلى الدماغ ومن الدماغ إلى فوق وكان هذا الشعر ناميًا على الدوام لأن البخار يتصاعد إلى الرأس أبدًا وهو مادة الشعر فبنماء الشعر ينمو البخار وكان فيه تخليص للبدن من تلك المواد وتكثير لوقايته وغطائه.

(فصل)

وأما شعر الحاجبين ففيه مع الحسن والزينة والجمال وقاية العين مما ينحدر من الرأس وجعل على هذا المقدار لأنه لو نقص عنه لزالت منفعة الجمال والوقاية ولو زاد عليه لغطى العين وأضر بها وحال بينها وبين ما تدركه وقد ذكرنا منفعة شعر الهدب.

ولما كان الأنفع والأصلح أن يكون شعر الهدب قاتما منتصبًا وأن يكون باقيًا على حال واحد في مقدار واحد جعل منبت هذا الشعر في جرم صلب شبيه بالغضروف يمتد في طول الجفن لئلا يطول وينمو وهذا كما نشاهد النبات الذي ينبت في الأرض الرخوة اللينة فإنه يطول ويزداد والذي ينبت في الأرض الصخرية الصلبة لا ينمو إلا نموًا يسيرًا فكذلك الشعر النابت في الأعضاء اللينة الرطبة فإنه سريع النمو كشعر الرأس والعانة.

(فصل)

وأما شعر اللحية ففيه منافع منها الزينة والوقار والهيبة ولهذا لا يرى على الصبيان والنساء من الهيبة والوقار ما يرى على ذوي اللحى ومنها التمييز بين الرجال والنساء.

فإن قيل لو كان شعر اللحية زينة لكان النساء أولى به من الرجال لحاجتهن إلى الزينة وكان التمييز يحصل بخلو الرجال منه ولكان أهل الجنة أولى به وقد ثبت أنهم جرد مرد.

قيل الجواب أن النساء لما كن محل الاستمتاع والتقبيل كان الأحسن والأولى خلوهن عن اللحى فإن محل الاستمتاع إذا خلا عن الشعر كان أتم ولهذا المعنى والله أعلم كان أهل الجنة مردًا ليكمل استمتاع نسائهم بهم كما يكمل استمتاعهم بهن وأيضًا فإنه أكشف لمحاسن الوجوه فإن الشعر يستر ما تحته من البشرة أن يمس بشرة المرأة والله أعلم بحكمته في خلقه.

(فصل)

وأما شعر العانة والإبط والأنف فمنفعته تنقية البدن من الفضلة ولهذا إذا أزيل من هذا الموضع وجد البدن خفة ونشاطًا وإذا وفر وجد ثقلًا وكسلًا وغمًا ولهذا جاءت الشريعة بحلق العانة ونتف الإبط وكان حلق العانة أولى من نتفها لصلابة الشعر وتأذي صاحبها بنتفه وكان نتف الإبط أولى من حلقه لضعف الشعر هناك وشدته وتعجل نباته بالحلق فجاءت الشريعة بالأنفع في هذا وهذا.

(فصل)

وتأمل حكمة الرب تعالى في كونه أخلى الكفين والجبهة والأخمصين من الشعر فإن الكفين خلقا حاكمين على الملموسات فلو حصل الشعر فيها لأخل بذلك وخلقا للقبض وإلصاق اللحم على المقبوض أعون على جودته من التصاف الشعر به وأيضًا فإنهما آلة الأخذ والعطاء والأكل ووجود الشعر فيهما يخل بتمام هذه المنفعة.

وأما الأخمصان فلو نبت الشعر فيهما لأضر بالماشي وأعاقه في المشي كثيرًا مما يعلق بشعره مما على الأرض ويتعلق شعره بما عليها أيضًا هذا مع أن أكثر الأوتار والأغشية في الكفين مانع من نفوذ الأبخرة فيها وأما الأخمصين فإن الأبخرة تتصاعد إلى علو وكلما تصاعد كان الشعر أكثر وأيضًا فإن كثرة وطء الأرض بالأخمصين يصلبهما ويجعل سطحهما أملس لا ينبت شيئًا كما أن الأرض التي توطأ كثيرًا لا تنبت شيئا وأما الجبهة فلو بنت الشعر عليها لستر محاسنها وأظلم الوجه وتدلى على العين وكان يحتاج إلى حلقه دائمًا ومنع العينين من كمال الإدراك والسبب المؤدي لذلك أن الذي تحت عظم الجبهة هو مقدم الدماغ وهو بارد رطب والبخار لا يتحرك منحرفًا إلى الجبهة بل صاعدًا إلى فوق.

فإن قيل لم نبت شعر الصبي على رأسه وحاجبيه وأجفانه معه من الصغر دون سائر الشعور.

قيل لشدة الحاجة إلى هذه الشعور الثلاثة أوجدها الله سبحانه معه وهو جنين في بطن أمه فإن شعر الرأس كالغطاء الواقي له من الآفات والأهداب والأجفان وقاية للعين.

فإن قيل فلم لم تنبت له اللحية إلا بعد بلوغه.

قيل لأنه عند البلوغ تجتمع الحرارة في بدنه وتكون أقوى ما هي ولهذا يعرض له في مثل هذا الطور البثرات والدمامل وكثرة الإحتلام وإذا كثرت الحرارة كثرة الأبخرة بسبب التحلل وزادت على القدر المحتاج إليه في شعر الرأس فصرفها أحكم الحاكمين إلى نبات اللحية والعانة وأيضًا فإن بين أوعية المنى وبين اللحية ارتباط إذ العروق والمجاري متصلة بينهما فإذا تعطلت أوعية المنى ويبست تعطل شعر اللحية وإذا قلت الرطوبة والحرارة هناك قل شعر اللحية، ولهذا فإن الخصيان لا ينبت لهم لحى فإن قيل فما العلة في الكوسج؟

قيل برد مزاجه ونقصان حرارته.

فإن قيل فما السبب في الصلع؟

قيل عدم احتباس الأبخرة في موضع الصلع.

فإن قيل فلم كان في مقدم الرأس دون جوانبه ومؤخره؟

قيل لأن الجزء المقدم من الرأس بسبب رطوبة الدماغ يكون أكثر لينًا وتحللًا فتتحلل الفضلات التي يكون منها الشعر فلا يبقى للشعر مادة هناك.

فإن قيل فلم لم يحدث في الأصداغ؟

قيل إن الرطوبة في الأسافل أكثر منها في الأعالي وشاهده الأرض العالية والمنخفضة.

فإن قيل فلم لم تصلع المرأة إلا نادرًا وكان الصلع في الرجال أكثر؟

قيل لأن الأصل أنه يحدث من يبس في الجلد بمنزلة احتراقه ذلك لقوة الحرارة وأما النساء فالرطوبة والبرودة أغلب عليهن ولهذا فإن جلودهن أرطب من جلود الرجال فلا تجف جلود رؤوسهن فلا يعرض لهن الصلح، ولهذا لا يعرض للصبيان وإن عرض للمرأة صلع فذلك في سن يبسها وبلوغها من الكبر عتيًا.

فإن قيل فما السبب في شدة سواد الشعر؟

قيل شدة البخارات الخارجة من البدن واعتدالها وصحة مادتها كخضرة الزرع.

فإن قيل ما سبب الصهوبة قيل برد المزاج فتضعف الحرارة عن صبغ الشعر وتسويده فإن قيل فما سبب الشقرة والحمرة؟

قيل زيادة الحرارة فتصبغ الشعر ولهذا تجد الشقر أشد حرارة وأكثر حركة وهمة.

فإن قيل فما سبب البياض؟

قيل البياض نوعان أحدهما طبيعي وهو الشيب والثاني خارج عن الطبيعة وهو ما يوجد في أواخر الأمراض المجففة بسبب تحلل الرطوبات كما يعرض للنبات عند الجفاف.

فإن قيل فما سبب الطبيعي؟

قيل اختلف في ذلك فقالت طائفة سببه الاستحالة إلى لون البلغم بسبب ضعف الحرارة في أبدان الشيوخ وقالت طائفة سببه أن الغذاء الصائر إلى الشعر يصير باردًا بسبب نقصان الحرارة ويكون بطيء الحركة مدة نفوذه إلى المسام وجمعت طائفة بين القولين وقالوا العلة في الأمرين واحدة وسببها نقصان الحرارة.

فإن قيل فلم اختص الشيب بالإنسان من بين سائر الحيوان؟

قيل لأن لحم الإنسان وجلده رخوين وجلود الحيوانات ولحومها أقوى واصلب فلما غلظت مادة الشعر فيها لم يعرض له ما يعرض لشعر الإنسان ولهذا يكون شعرها كلها معها من حين ولادتها بخلاف الإنسان وأيضا فإن لإنسان? المركبة المتنوعة وكذا المشارب ويتناول أكثر من حاجته فتجتمع فيه فضلات كثيرة فتدفعها الطبيعة إلى ظاهر البدن فما دامت الحرارة قوية فإنه تقوى على إحراق تلك الفضلات فيتولد من إحراقها الشعر الأسود فإذا بلغ الشيخوخة ضعفت الحرارة وعجزت عن إحراق تلك الفضلات فتعمل فيها عملًا ضعيفًا وأما سائر الحيوانات فلا تتناول الأغذية المركبة وتتناول منها على قدر الحاجة فلا يشيب شعرها كما يشيب شعر الإنسان وأيضًا فإن في زمن الشيخوخة يكون أقل حرارة وأكثر رطوبة فيتولد البلغم وأما الحيوانات فاليبس غالب عليها.

فإن قيل فلم كان شيب الأصداغ في الأكثر مقدمًا على غيره؟

قيل لقرب هذا الموضع من مقدم الدماغ والرطوبة في مقدم الدماغ كثيرة لأن الموضع مفصل والمفصل تجتمع فيه الفضلة الكثيرة فيكثر البرد هناك فيسرع الشيب.

فإن قيل فلم أسرع الشيب في شعور في شعور الخصيان والنساء قيل أما النساء فلبرد مزاجهن في الأصل ولاجتماع الفضلات الكثيرة فيهن وأما الخصيان فلتوافر المنى على أبدانهم يصير دمهم غليظا بلغميا ولهذا لا يحدث الصلع.

فإن قيل فلم كان شعر الإبط لا يبيض؟

قيل لقوة حرارة هذا الموضع بسبب قربه من القلب ومسامه كثيرة بلغمية لأنها تتحلل بالعرق الدائم.

فإن قيل فلم أبطأ بياض شعر العانة قيل لأن حركة الجماع تحلل البلغم الذي في مسامه.

فإن قيل فلم كانت الحيوانات تتبدل شعورها كل سنة بخلاف الإنسان قيل لضعف شعورها عن الدوام والبقاء بخلاف شعر الآدمي.

فإن قيل فما سبب الجعودة والسبوطة؟

قيل أما الجعودة فمن شدة الحرارة أو من التواء المسام فالذي من شدة الحرارة فإنه تعرض منه الجعودة كما تعرض الشعر عند عرضه على النار وأما الذي لالتواء المسام فلأن البخار لضعفه لا يقدر أن ينفذ على الاستقامة فيلتوي في المنافذ فتحدث الجعودة.

فإن قيل فما السبب في طول شعر الميت وأظفاره بعد موته إذا بقي مدة؟

قيل عنه جوابان أحدهما أنها لا تطول ولكن لما ينقص ما حولها يظن أنها زادت.

الثاني وهو أصوب أن ذلك الطول من الفضلات البخارية التي تتحلل وهلة من الميت فيمتد معها الشعر والظفر.

فإن قيل فلم كان المريض وخاصة المحموم ينقص لحمه ويزيد شعره؟

قيل إن في المرض تكثر الفضلات فتطول الشعور والأظفار بها ويثقل الغذاء فيذوب اللجم.

وأما في الصحة فتقل الفضلات فلا تحتاج الطبيعة إلى الغذاء وهضمها له.

وإذا قلت الفضلات نفدت مادة الشعر فيبطئ.

فإن قيل فما العلة في انتصاب شعر الخائف والمقرور حتى يبقى كشعر القنفذ؟

قيل العلة فيه أن الجلد ينقبض وتجتمع المسام على الشعر وتتضايق عليه فينتصب فإن قيل: فلم انتصب شعر البدن واللحية واللحيين؟

قيل: لأن جلدة "الرأس" كثيفة أكثف من جلدة البدن فلا تنقبض انقباض جلدة البدن، على أن شعر "الرأس" - أيضا - ينتصب كذلك، وإن كان دون انتصاب شعر البدن و"اللحية ".

فإن قيل فلم كانت كثرة الجماع تزيد في شعر اللحية والجسد وتنقص من شعر الرأس والأجفان؟

قيل لأن الشعر فيه ما يكون طبيعيًا من أول الخلقة كاللحية وسائر شعر البدن والأول يكون من قوة الحرارة الأصلية والثاني من قوة الحرارة الخارجية فلا جرم نقصت بسببه الشعور الأصلية وتوفرت العرضية.

فإن قيل فلم كان الشعر في الإنسان في الجزء المقدم أكثر منه في المؤخر وباقي الحيوانات بالعكس؟

قيل لأن الشعر إنما يكون حيث تكون الحرارة قوية ويكون تحلل الجلد أكثر، وهذا في الإنسان في ناحية الصدر والبطن.

وأما جلدة الظهر فمتكاثفة، وأما ذوات الأربع ففي الخلف شعورها أكثر لأن البخار فيها يرقى إلى الخلف وإن تلك المواضع هي التي تتلقى الحر والبرز فتحتاج إلى وقاء أكثر.

فإن قيل فلم كان الرأس بالشعر أحق الأعضاء ونباته أكثر؟

قيل لأن البخار يتصاعد ويطلب جهة الفوق وهو الرأس.

ولا تستطل هذا الفصل فإن أمر الشعر من السمات والفضلات وهذا شأنه فما الظن بغيره من الأجزاء الأصلية فإذا كانت هذه قليلة من كثير من حكمة الرب تعالى في الشعور ومواضعها ومنافعها فكيف بحكمته في الرأس والقلب والكبد والصدر وغيرها ولا تضجر من ذلك فإن الخلق فيه من الفقه والحكم نظير ما في الأمر فالرب تعالى حكيم في خلقه وأمره ويحب من يفقه عنه ذلك ويستدل على كمال حكمته وعلمه ولطفه وتدبيره فإذا كان الله لم يضع هذه الفضلات في الإنسان سدى فما الظن بغيرها.

(فصل)

ونحن نذكر فصلًا مختصرًا في حال الإنسان من مبدئه إلى نهايته لنجعله مرآة له ينظر فيها قول خالقه وبارئه ﴿وَفِي أنْفُسِكم أفَلا تُبْصِرُونَ﴾

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 51, verse 21 (part 3 of 15):

When the perfection of the Lord, exalted is His majesty, along with His complete power, all-encompassing knowledge, executing will, and profound wisdom required the diversification of His creation from differing materials, and the bringing of them into existence in different forms, and the great disparity among them in materials, forms, attributes, configurations, shapes, natures and faculties, His wisdom required that He take a handful of dust from the earth, then pour water upon it, so it became like black, moulded clay (al-hama' al-masnun). Then He sent the wind upon it, which dried it until it became dry clay like pottery (salsal ka'l-fakhkhar). Then He decreed for it its limbs, its openings, its joints, and its moisture, and fashioned it. He originated its shaping and displayed it in the best of forms. He articulated it in the finest articulation while its parts remained connected, and He prepared each part for what was intended from it, and measured it for what it was created, in the most eloquent manner. Thus He articulated it in its joining and originated its shaping and formation. The angels saw it but did not know what was intended for it, and Iblis circled around it, saying, "For some matter this was created." 

When its shaping and formation were complete, and the measuring of its limbs and joints was perfected, and it became a fashioned, formed body, as if it spoke, except that there was no spirit in it and no life, He sent to it His spirit, and He breathed into it a breath, and that clay turned into flesh, blood, bones, veins, hearing, sight, smell, touch, movement and speech. The first thing with which it began was to say, "Al-hamdu lillahi rabbi al-'alamin (All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds)." Then its Creator, Originator and Fashioner said to it, "May Allah have mercy on you, O Adam." Then he sat up, the most beautiful thing, the most splendid in appearance, the most perfect in creation, and the most originated in form. 

The Lord, exalted is He, said to all His angels, ﴿Prostrate to Adam﴾, so they hastened to prostrate, in glorification and obedience to the command of the One, the Worshipped. Then He said to them: "In this handful of dust We have a form more wondrous than what you see, and an inner beauty more lovely than what you perceive. Adorning its inner self is more excellent than the adornment of its outer self. We shall make it one of Our greatest signs. We shall teach it the names of everything, which the angels cannot do well." So teaching was the adornment and beauty of the inner self, and that shaping was the adornment of the outer self, in the most perfect and beautiful form and meaning. All of that is His making, blessed and exalted, in a handful of dust. Then from it He derived a form which is like it in beauty and loveliness, so that he might find rest in her, his soul be at ease, and from the two of them there would emerge countless men and women besides them.

(Section)

Then, when Allah, glorified is He, willed to scatter their offspring upon the earth and multiply them, He placed in them the heat of desire, the fire of longing and seeking, and inspired each of them to unite with his or her partner. So they came together upon a matter already decreed. Now listen to the wonders that are there.

When the Lord, exalted is He, willed to bring forth the essence of this human from him, He deposited in his body a heat and empowered its agitation, so it became an overwhelming desire. When the heat of the body is aroused, the moisture dissolves from all parts of the body and begins to descend from behind the brain, through the veins behind the ears, down to the nape of the back. Then it goes out to the two kidneys, then gathers in the vessels of semen, after the fire of desire has cooked it and thickened it until it gained consistency and density, and shortened it until it became white. He decreed for it channels and pathways through which it passes. Then His wisdom, glorified is He, required that He decree for its exit the most powerful causes that expel it from outside and from inside. So He made beautiful to the eye of the beholder the form of the other, and its longing for it, and drew one toward the other by the chain of desire and love. Each yearned to mix with its partner and to blend with it, so that Allah might accomplish a matter that was already done. He made this the place of tillage and that the place of seed, so that the two waters would meet upon a matter decreed. He decreed between them those movements so that the heat would act upon that moisture and the residue would do its work, and He extracted it from beneath the hair, skin and nails, so that it would match the original essence and the impulse to procreate would be at its utmost strength, so that offspring would not cease. For this reason you do not find in nocturnal emission the strength that is in intercourse; it is merely from an excess of heat that melts the moisture, so that nature passes through it to the outside, in a form of imagined vision through the agency of Satan, as in the Sahih, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said, "The good dream is from Allah and the nightmare is from Satan."

If it is said: this is your choice of the view of those who say that semen comes out from all parts of the body. Although many people have said this, others have opposed them and claimed that it is a residue produced from food, and it is one of the most balanced residues, and for this reason it is suitable to be the origin of a human, which is a body whose parts are alike in itself. It is said: the first view is the correct one, and it is indicated by several matters. Among them: the pleasure spreads through all parts of the body. Among them: the resemblance of the child's limbs to the limbs of the parents. Among them: the complete resemblance indicates that the whole body sent the semen; otherwise the resemblance would be according to a single place. This shows that every limb sent its portion and share. So when it was conceived and formed, its imitation and resemblance of it appeared. Among them: if the matter were as the proponents of the second view claim, that semen is one body alike in itself, then from it would not be produced the various limbs with different shapes, because one power does not act upon one matter except with one action. This shows that the matter in itself is not alike in its parts.

Among them: semen is the residue of the final digestion, and that occurs when the blood ripens in the veins and becomes fully prepared to turn into the substance of the limbs. Likewise, after its expulsion, weakness results more than from the expulsion of similar blood, and for this reason it causes weakness in the substance of the principal limbs. This shows that it is composed of parts of each, close to readiness to become a part of a limb. For this reason Allah called it sulalah, and sulalah is on the pattern of fa'alah from sall, which is what flows out of the body like vapour, just as He named its origin sulalah from clay, because He drew it out from all the earth, as in the Jami' of al-Tirmidhi from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Allah created Adam from a handful He took from all the earth."

The proponents of the other view, who are the majority of physicians and others, said: If the matter were as you claim, and semen is drawn from all the limbs, then when the male's semen and the female's semen enter the womb, the child would be formed in the shape of both of them together, and a man would only ever bear males, since semen, according to you, has been drawn from all his parts, so when it is conceived it must be like him. Also, a woman bears from a man's intercourse, in one womb, a male and a female, and it cannot be said that this is due to differences in the parts of the semen.

They said: We do not accept the generality of pleasure, because it occurs only at the moment of emission, through the flow of that hot substance along those fleshy channels whose flesh is soft, resembling fresh flesh that has just healed when something flows over it while it is moderately warm. And if the pleasure were caused by the flow of that substance, it would have occurred before emission. They said: As for your argument from the resemblance between parent and child, resemblance may occur in the nails and hair, and nothing is separated from them. Also, the child may resemble a distant ancestor, as is established in the Sahih from the Prophet (ﷺ), that a man asked him and said, "My wife has borne a black boy." He said, "Do you have camels?" He said, "Yes." He said, "What colour are they?" He said, "Black." He said, "Is there among them any grey?" He said, "Yes." He said, "Then how is that?" He said, "Perhaps a vein pulled it out." He said, "And perhaps this is a vein that pulled it out."

They said: If there were parts from every limb in the semen, then those parts must either be placed in the semen in their required arrangement or not. If they are placed in their required arrangement, the semen would be a small animal; and if not, the resemblance would be impossible. They said: Also, the semen either has the composition and arrangement of these limbs or not. The first is clearly false, since semen is a flowing moisture that does not retain placement and arrangement; and if it were thick, the second is determined, and it is certain that the arrangement, shaping and formation must be attributed to another cause besides the power in the substance, for it is a power without awareness, perception, or guidance to these details found in the human form. Rather, this shaping and formation is traced to an all-knowing, all-wise Creator, whose wisdom has dazzled minds, and whose signs of creation indicate the perfection of His names, attributes and oneness. The two eminent physicians, Hippocrates and Plato, acknowledged this, and they both affirmed that it is attributed to the wisdom and providence of the Maker, and that it proceeds only from a wise, knowing, powerful One. Galen related this from them in his book "The Opinion of Hippocrates and Plato." But the ignorant physicians and the heretic philosophers and naturalists refused except disbelief. And it is established in the Sahih from the Prophet (ﷺ), from the hadith of Hudhayfah ibn Usayd: "Allah has appointed over the womb an angel who says: O Lord, a drop; O Lord, a clot; O Lord, a lump. What is the sustenance, what is the term, what is the deed? Then Allah decrees what He wills, and the angel writes it." In another wording: "The angel who creates it," i.e., who shapes it by Allah's permission, shaping His creation in the wombs as Allah wills. There is no god but He, the Mighty, the Wise.

The proponents of the first view said: We have more right to declare Allah free of imperfection and to affirm His oneness, and to know the wisdom of the All-Knowing Creator, His power and His knowledge, and we are happier with that than you are, and anyone among our foolish and heretical ones who attributes this creation to a shaping power and natural causes, without attributing it to a free, all-knowing, all-powerful Agent, nothing occurs except by His permission and will. Power and nature are creatures subjected by His creation, a servant among His servants, having no action, movement or effect except by the permission of their Originator and Creator. Such a person has ignored himself and his Lord, and the custom of nature and of revelation. The Lord, exalted is He, creates what He wills, chooses, and shapes His creation in the wombs as He wills, by causes He has measured and wisdoms He has arranged. If He wills to strip those causes of their powers, He strips them; if He wills to cut off their effects from them, He cuts them off; and if He wills to prepare for them other causes that oppose and counteract them, He does so. He is the Doer of what He intends. The fact that semen is drawn from all parts of the body does not remove the matter from His power, will and wisdom; rather, that is more eloquent in wisdom and power.

As for your statement that if semen were drawn from all the limbs the child would be shaped in the shape of both together, the Prophet answered the one who asked about that with what suffices and satisfies. In the Sahih of al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: News reached 'Abd Allah ibn Salam of the Messenger of Allah's arrival in Madinah, while he was at his land working. He came to him and said, "I will ask you about three things that no one knows except a prophet: What is the first sign of the Hour? What is the first food the people of Paradise will eat? And from what does a child take after its father, and from what does it take after its maternal uncles?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "Jibril just now informed me of them." 'Abd Allah said, "He is the enemy of the Jews among the angels." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "As for the first sign of the Hour, it is a fire that will gather people from the east to the west. As for the first food of the people of Paradise, it is the caudate lobe of the fish's liver. As for the resemblance in the child: if a man covers a woman and his water precedes hers, the child resembles him; and if her water precedes his, it resembles her." He said, "I bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah." So this is the answer of Jibril, the trustworthy, the Lord of the worlds, not the answer of Jibril the physician. In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Thawban, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "If the man's water overcomes the woman's, the child is male by Allah's permission; and if the woman's water overcomes the man's, the child is female by Allah's permission." Sometimes the two waters are equal in emission and quantity, and that is among the rarest things, so the child is created with a male's member like a man's and a female's genitalia like a woman's. If Allah wills to make the male's semen-essence prevail over the woman's or her essence, He commands the angel of the wombs to shape it accordingly. This does not contradict His wisdom nor break His custom; and even if He broke it, that would not compromise the wisdom of the Wisest of judges.

As for your denial of the generality of pleasure, it is close to obstinacy. The one who copulates finds at the moment of emission something drawn from his whole body, hearing, sight and faculties, into the mould of the womb, so he feels as if he has taken off a shirt he was wrapped in. For this reason the wisdom of the Lord, exalted is He, in His law and decree, required that He commanded him to perform ghusl after that, so that water would replace what was dissolved from his body. When he washes, he finds vigour and strength, as if nothing was lost from him. The moisture of water replaces on the body what that movement dissolved from its moistures, and the innate heat acts upon it, supplying the powers that weakened by the emission.

As for the resemblance occurring between the nail and the hair in parent and child, with nothing separating them: how weak that objection is. The nail and hair follow the limbs and the temperament in which the resemblance occurred, so the resemblance of the origin brought the resemblance of what follows it.

As for the resemblance of the child to a distant ancestor, it is among our strongest proofs on this question, because that distant resemblance kept moving through the loins until it settled in the form of the child, and through it the resemblance was achieved.

As for your statement that those parts either are placed in the semen in their required arrangement or not, and so on to the end: our answer is that if you mean they are placed actually, that is not so; and if you mean they are placed potentially, then yes, and what prevents that? The semen would be a small animal, indeed a large one potentially. By this the answer becomes clear to your claim that semen is a flowing moisture that does not retain placement and arrangement. The most that can be granted is that this is a part of the causes by which Allah creates the child, and a part of a cause does not independently decide the matter. The one who alone brings things into existence is the will of Allah alone, and causes are the places where it appears.

(Section)

If it is said: this is your explicit statement that the woman also has semen, and that from her is one of the two components from which Allah creates the child. Some physicians thought that the woman has no semen?

It is said: this is the very question which Mother of the Believers 'A'ishah and Umm Salamah (may Allah be pleased with them) raised before the Prophet (ﷺ). He answered them by affirming the woman's semen. In the Sahih, Umm Sulaym (may Allah be pleased with her) said, "O Messenger of Allah, Allah is not shy of the truth. Does a woman have to perform ghusl if she has a wet dream?" He said, "Yes, if she sees the water." Umm Salamah said, "Does a woman have wet dreams?" He said, "May your hands be dust! Then how does the child resemble her?"

In both of them, from 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her): Umm Sulaym (may Allah be pleased with her) asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about a woman who sees in her dream what a man sees; must she perform ghusl? He said, "Yes, if she sees the water." She said, "I said to him: Does a woman experience that?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "Then how could the resemblance come about except through that? When her water overcomes the man's water, the child resembles his maternal uncles; and when the man's water overcomes hers, the child resembles his paternal uncles." This is the wording of Muslim.

Galen criticized Aristotle, since he said that a woman has no semen. Let us now examine this question medically as we have examined it legally, and we say: The male's semen is among the moistures and residues in the body, and this is something that is shared between male and female, from which the child is formed, and through which the resemblance comes about. Had the woman had no semen, the child would not resemble her.

It cannot be said that the cause of resemblance is menstrual blood, for it does not combine with the man's semen nor unite with it.

Ibn al-Qayyim's commentary on surah 51, verse 21 (part 4 of 15):

God has established the custom that procreation occurs only between two origins, from which a third is produced. The seed (mani) of the man alone does not produce a child unless it is mixed with another substance from the female. Those who hold the other view have acknowledged this, and they said that there must be a white, viscous substance from the woman which becomes the substance of the fetus's body. But they disputed whether it possesses a binding force (quwwa 'aqida) as the man's seed does, or not. The Prophet ﷺ touched upon this question in the hadith narrated by Muslim in his Sahih from the hadith of Thawban, his freedman, when the Jews asked him about the child. He said: "The water of the man is white and the water of the woman is yellow. When they meet, if the man's water overcomes the woman's water, the child will be male by God's permission; and if the woman's water overcomes the man's water, the child will be female by God's permission." Indeed, the man's seed alone has thickness, whiteness, and emission with spurting and force, and the woman's seed alone has thinness, yellowness, and flowing without force. If one who denies the woman's seed intends to deny these attributes for it, he is correct; but if he denies that, he is mistaken. Each of the two waters has a force, and when one joins the other they acquire a third force, which is among the causes of the formation of the fetus. The wisdom of the All-Knowing Creator, glory be to Him, required that the inside of the womb be rough like a sponge, and that it have a craving for the seed and an acceptance of it, like the craving of parched earth for water and its acceptance of it. So He made it seeking, retaining, and longing for it due to thirst. Therefore, when it obtains it, it embraces it and does not waste it, but encloses it with the utmost enclosure, and contracts with the greatest contraction lest the air corrupt it. The force and heat there are in charge, by God's permission, under the angel of the womb. When it encloses the seed and does not expel it outward, it turns around upon itself and becomes like a sphere, and it continues to solidify for six full days. When it has solidified, a point appears at its center, the place of the heart, and a point at its top, the point of the brain, and one on the right, the point of the liver. Then those points separate and red lines appear between them for three more days. Then blood flows through all of it after six more days, so that totals fifteen days, and the total becomes twenty-seven days. Then the head separates from the shoulders, the extremities from the ribs, and the belly from the forehead, and that is in nine days, so it becomes thirty-six days. Then this distinction is completed, so that it becomes clearly visible to the senses in four days, and the total becomes forty days, during which its form is gathered together. This agrees with the words of the Prophet ﷺ in the hadith agreed upon as authentic: "Indeed, one of you has his creation gathered in his mother's womb for forty days." The Prophet was content with this summary instead of detail. This indicates that God has gathered its creation in a hidden gathering, and that creation becomes apparent gradually and in a hidden manner. Then it becomes a lump of flesh for another forty days, and this formation increases little by little until it becomes visible to the senses with a clarity that conceals nothing of it. The spirit has not yet been attached to it, for it is only attached to it in the fourth forty, after a hundred and twenty days, as the Truthful one has informed us. This is something that cannot be known except through revelation, since nature does not require it. Therefore the excellent physicians and the brilliant philosophers were perplexed about it, and they said that this is something that cannot be known except by distant conjecture. One who has investigated the ends of their statements on this matter, and exerted himself in it until he was exhausted, and he is the author of al-Tibb al-Kabir, mentioned imaginary analogies, then said: "The reality of knowledge concerning it is with God, exalted is He; no one among creatures has any hope of comprehending it."

I say: The Truthful, the Believed, who does not speak from desire, has informed us of it in what is established in the two Sahihs: "Indeed, the creation of one of you is gathered in his mother's womb for forty days, then he becomes a clot of blood for a similar period, then a lump of flesh for a similar period, then the angel is sent to him and he breathes the spirit into him, and he is commanded with four matters: to write his provision, his term of life, his deeds, and whether he is wretched or happy."

(Section)

I have seen a statement by some physicians which mentions the cause of the variation in the time of birth, so I will mention it and mention what is in it.

He said: When the creation of the fetus is complete in a specific period, then if a similar period passes beyond it, the fetus moves. When twice that is added to the total, the fetus is separated. He said: When its creation is completed in thirty days, then when it has sixty days it moves; when twice the sixty is added, it becomes a hundred and eighty days, which is six months, and that is the period at which the pregnancy is separated. If its creation is completed in thirty-five days, it moves at seventy and is separated at seven months. If its creation is completed at forty, it moves at eighty and is separated at eight months. If it is completed at forty-five, it moves at ninety and is separated at nine months. And so on by this calculation always. This statement of this speaker implies movement of the fetus before the fortieth day, and this is definitely an error, for the spirit is only attached to it after the third forty, and only then does it move. Therefore no movement of its own is established before a hundred and twenty days. Whatever movement is estimated before that is not a self-originated, voluntary movement, but perhaps an accidental movement caused by the membranes and fluids. The calculation he mentioned is supported by neither evidence nor consistent experience; it may exceed that or fall short of it. What we are certain of is that the spirit is not attached to it until after the third forty. Whatever movement is estimated before that, if it is valid, was not caused by the spirit. And God knows best.

(Section)

As for the minimum period of pregnancy, the Sharia and nature agree that it is six months. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And its carrying and its weaning is thirty months﴾.

And He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And mothers suckle their children for two complete years, for those who wish to complete the suckling﴾.

Galen said: I was very diligent in investigating the durations of the periods of pregnancy, and I saw one woman who gave birth after a hundred and eighty-four nights. The author of al-Shifa claimed that he witnessed this. As for the maximum, he said in al-Shifa: "It reached me, from a source I trust, that a woman gave birth after the fourth [year] from the beginning of the pregnancy to a child whose teeth had grown, and he lived."

(Section)

If it is asked: what is the cause of the production of males and females?

It is said: What we choose is that its cause is the will of the Lord, the Doer, by His choice, and it is not a natural cause. Everything the proponents of natures have mentioned concerning the begetting of males is refuted, such as the heat and moisture of the man. They said that corruption of temperament also necessitates the begetting of females, and its soundness necessitates the begetting of males. This is confusion and nonsense. There is no cause for males and females except the word of God to the angel of the wombs, who asks: "O Lord, male? O Lord, female? O Lord, wretched or happy? What is the provision? What is the term? And males and females, what accompanies happiness and wretchedness, provision and term?"

If it is asked: are those also by causes?

We say: Yes, but by causes after birth, and there is no cause for males and females before birth.

If it is asked: what do you make of the hadith of Thawban narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, that a Jew asked the Prophet ﷺ about the child, and he said: "The water of the man is white and the water of the woman is yellow. When they meet, if the man's water overcomes the woman's water, the child will be male by God's permission; and if the woman's water overcomes the man's water, the child will be female by God's permission." Then the Jew said: "You have spoken the truth, and you are indeed a Prophet." It is said: this hadith is reported exclusively by Muslim in his Sahih, and some have criticized it, saying that it is apparent that the hadith is an error by some narrators, and that the question was actually about the resemblance, which is what Abdullah ibn Salam asked about in the hadith agreed upon as authentic, and he answered him with the precedence of the water, for resemblance belongs to the one whose water precedes. Perhaps some narrator confused the resemblance of the child to the mother with being female, and its resemblance to the father with being male, especially since complete resemblance is only through that.

Another group said: the hadith is sound, with no flaw in its chain, and there is no contradiction between it and the hadith of Abdullah ibn Salam; the incident is not one but two separate events, and the narration of each is different from the other.

The hadith of Thawban contains a recorded and memorized incident. Thawban said: I was standing with the Messenger of God ﷺ when a rabbi of the Jewish rabbis came and said: "Peace be upon you, O Muhammad." So I pushed him with a push that nearly knocked him down. He said to me: "Why did you push me?" I said: "Will you not say, 'O Messenger of God!'" The Jew said: "We only call him by the name his family gave him." The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "My name is Muhammad, which my family gave me." The Jew said: "I came to ask you." The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Will anything benefit you if I tell you?" He said: "I will listen with my ears." The Messenger of God ﷺ scratched the ground with a stick he had with him. The Jew said: "Where will people be on the day the earth is changed to other than the earth, and the heavens?" The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "They will be in darkness, beyond the Bridge." He said: "Who will be the first to be permitted?" He said: "The poor among the Emigrants." He said: "What will be their gift before they enter Paradise?" He said: "The extra piece of the fish's liver." He said: "What will be their food after it?" He said: "The Bull of Paradise will be slaughtered for them, which eats from its outskirts." He said: "What will be their drink with it?" He said: "From a spring in it called Salsabil." He said: "You have spoken the truth." He said: "I also came to ask you about something no one knows except a prophet, or a man, or two men." He said: "Will it benefit you if I tell you?" He said: "I will listen with my ears." He said: "I came to ask you about the child?" He said: "The water of the man is white and the water of the woman is yellow. When they meet, if the man's water overcomes the woman's water, the child will be male by God's permission; and if the woman's water overcomes the man's water, the child will be female by God's permission." The Jew said: "You have indeed spoken the truth, and you are indeed a Prophet," then he left. The Messenger of God ﷺ said, after he had gone: "This one asked me what he asked, and I had no knowledge of it until God brought it to me."

As for the hadith of Abdullah ibn Salam, may God be pleased with him, it is in Sahih al-Bukhari from Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: News of the arrival of the Messenger of God ﷺ in Medina reached Abdullah ibn Salam, so he came to him and said: "I will ask you about three things that only a prophet knows: What is the first sign of the Hour? What is the first food the people of Paradise eat? And from what does a child draw resemblance to its father, and from what does it draw resemblance to its maternal uncles?" The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Gabriel has just informed me of them." Abdullah said: "That is the enemy of the Jews among the angels." He said: "As for the first sign of the Hour, it is a fire that gathers people from the east to the west. As for the first food the people of Paradise eat, it is the extra piece of the fish's liver. As for resemblance in the child: when a man covers a woman and his water precedes hers, the resemblance is to him; and when her water precedes, the resemblance is to her." He said: "I bear witness that you are the Messenger of God," and he mentioned the hadith.

The two hadiths thus include two matters, with two results following together, and each one alone produces its own result. If the man's water precedes and overcomes, the child is male and resembles him. If the woman's water precedes and overcomes, the child is female and resembles her. If the woman's water precedes and the man's water overcomes, the child is male and resembles her. Yet even with all this, this is a part of a cause, not a necessitating cause, and the necessitating cause is the will of God. He may make a cause produce the opposite of its effect, and He may cause the opposite of its normal result, and this is no contradiction to His wisdom, just as it is not a limitation of His power. He has indicated this in the hadith with His words: "male by God's permission" and "female by God's permission." God, the Exalted, says: ﴿To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills. He bestows females upon whom He wills, and He bestows males upon whom He wills, or He pairs them, males and females, and He makes whom He wills barren. Indeed, He is All-Knowing, All-Powerful﴾.

So He, glory be to Him, informed that this returns to His will, that He may grant males only, females only, and that He may give parents both kinds together, or leave them both without either. Just as it returns to His will, it is connected to His knowledge and power. God gave Adam males and females, gave Israel males only and not females, and gave Muhammad females only except for his son Ibrahim. Solomon, peace be upon him, said: "Tonight I will go around to seventy women, and each will bear a boy who will fight in the way of God." He went around to them, but only one woman bore, and she brought forth half a child. The Prophet ﷺ said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, if he had said 'if God wills,' they would have fought in the way of God as horsemen, all of them." This shows that mere intercourse is not a complete cause, though it has a part in causation, and that the complete cause is the will of God alone. He is the Lord of causes, who disposes of them as He wills: granting them causal power when He wills, withholding it when He wills, and bringing about the opposite of their normal effect when He wills. Causes are the channels of the Sharia and of decree, and upon them the command of God, both cosmic and religious, proceeds.

If it is asked: it has become clear that the child is created from both waters together; so is it created from the two equally, or is the child from the father's water and part from the mother's water?

It is said: The Prophet ﷺ has explained this question in the clearest manner. Imam Ahmad said in his Musnad: Husayn ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Abu Kurayb narrated to us, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: A Jew passed by the Messenger of God while he was talking to his companions. The Quraysh said: "O Jew, this man claims to be a prophet." He said: "I will ask him about something only a prophet knows." He came, sat down, and said: "O Muhammad, from what is man created?" He said: "From each: man is created from the seed of the man and the seed of the woman. As for the man's seed, it is a thick seed, from which come the bones and sinews; and as for the woman's seed, it is a thin seed, from which come the flesh and blood." The Jew stood up and said: "This is what those before you say."

(Section)

If it is asked: you have mentioned that the spirit is attached to the fetus only after the third forty, and that the creation of the fetus is gathered in its mother's womb for forty days, then a clot for a similar period, then a lump of flesh for a similar period; and you have shown that the statements of the physicians do not contradict what revelation has informed us of. So what do you make of the hadith of Hudhayfah ibn Usayd, narrated by Muslim in his Sahih from the Prophet, who said: "The angel enters the drop after it settles in the womb by forty or forty-five nights, and says: 'O Lord, wretched or happy?' and they both write it down. Then he says: 'O Lord, male or female?' and they both write it down, and he records his deeds, his traces, his term, and his provision. Then he rolls up the scroll, and nothing is added to it or subtracted from it." It is said: we receive this with acceptance and affirmation, and we leave aside distortion. It does not contradict what we have mentioned, for at most it says that the decree occurred after the first forty, while the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud indicates that it occurred after the third forty, and both are true, as the Truthful one said. This is a decree after a decree. The first is a decree at the transfer of the drop to the first stage of formation, which is the first stage of the human being; before that, formation had not been attached to it. The second decree is at the completion of its creation and the breathing of the spirit, so that is a decree at the completion of its form and shaping. This is better than the answer of those who say that the forty meant in the hadith of Hudhayfah is the third forty, which is very far from the wording of the hadith, and its wording rejects it utterly. So reflect on it.

If it is asked: what do you make of his other hadith in Sahih Muslim from Amir ibn Wathila, that he heard Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may God be pleased with him, say: "The wretched one is he who is wretched in his mother's womb, and the happy one is he who is admonished by others." He came to a man among the Companions of the Prophet called Hudhayfah ibn Usayd al-Ghifari, and related this to him as a statement of Ibn Mas'ud, and said to him: "How can a man be wretched without deeds?" The man said to him: "Are you surprised at that? I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say:
"When two and forty nights pass over the drop, God sends to it an angel who shapes it, creates its hearing, sight, skin, flesh, and bones, then says: 'O Lord, male or female?' Your Lord decrees what He wills, and the angel writes it on the scroll in his hand, and adds nothing to his command or subtracts from it."

In another wording, also in the Sahih, I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ with these two ears of mine say:
"Indeed the drop falls into the womb for forty nights, then the angel who creates it comes to it and says: 'O Lord, male or female? Well-formed or not well-formed?' God makes it well-formed or not well-formed. Then he says: 'O Lord, what is its provision, what is its term, and what is its creation?' Then God, the Mighty and Majestic, makes it wretched or happy."

In another wording, also in the Sahih:
"Indeed, an angel is appointed over the womb, and when God wishes to create something, by God's permission, it is for about forty-some nights..."

Then he mentioned something similar.

It is said: we receive this too with affirmation and acceptance, and we leave aside distortion. This agrees with what the physicians unanimously agree upon, that the beginning of formation and shaping is after the forty

Ibn al-Qayyim's Tafsir (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 51, verse 21 (part 5 of 15):

If it is said: How can this be reconciled with the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, which is explicit that the drop (nutfah) remains a drop for forty days, then a clot ('alaqah) for forty days, then a lump of flesh (mudghah) for forty days? And it is known that the clot and the lump have no form in them, no skin, no flesh, and no bone. We have no need to reconcile his hadith with the statements of the physicians, for the word of the Prophet is infallible, whereas theirs is liable to error. Rather, the need is to reconcile his hadith with the earlier hadith of Hudhayfah.

It is said: There is no contradiction between the two hadiths, praise be to Allah, and both have come forth from a truthful, infallible source. Some have thought that the shaping (tasweer) in the hadith of Hudhayfah occurs only after the third forty days. They said: The most that it contains is the particle fa' (فَ) indicating sequence, and the sequence of each thing is according to its nature. Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green?﴾ Indeed, Allah the Exalted has also said: ﴿Then We made the drop a clot, then We made the clot a lump, then We made the lump bones, then We clothed the bones with flesh﴾. This is sequence according to what the situation allows, and it does not follow that the second must come immediately after the first.

Others have thought that the shaping and creating in the hadith of Hudhayfah refers to the decree and knowledge, while what is in the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud refers to external existence. The correct view, which is indicated by the hadith, is that the determination is in the second forty days. However, there are here two kinds of shaping: one is a hidden shaping that does not appear, which is a shaping by decree, as when you cut a garment or carve a door, marking the places of cutting and division, and placing the points of separation and joining. Likewise, whoever places a form in a material, especially a form like this, produces the shaping and creating in it gradually, little by little, and not all at once, as is observed with the eye in the visible formation within an egg.

So there are here four stages. The first is a knowing shaping and creating that has not yet come out into external existence. The second is the beginning of a hidden shaping that the senses are unable to perceive. The third is a shaping that the senses can reach but which is not yet complete. The fourth is the completion of the shaping, after which there remains only the breathing in of the spirit (nafkh al-ruh).

The first stage is a knowledge, and the other three are external and concrete. This shaping following a shaping is like a decree following a decree. The Lord, Exalted is He, decreed the measures of creation with a general decree fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth, and in it were written the records of happiness and misery, deeds, provisions, and terms of life. The second is a decree after this, and it is more specific: the decree that took place at the two handfuls, when Allah, Blessed and Exalted, grasped the people of happiness with His right hand and said, "These are for Paradise, and they will do the deeds of the people of Paradise," and grasped the people of misery with the other hand and said, "These are for the Fire, and they will do the deeds of the people of the Fire." The third is a decree after this, more specific still, at the time when the person is conceived, as in the hadith of Hudhayfah ibn Usayd that was mentioned. The fourth is another decree after this, which is at the time when its creation is completed and the spirit is breathed into it, as the hadith before it stated explicitly. This indicates the breadth of the knowledge of the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, and His comprehensiveness regarding universals and particulars. Likewise, the second shaping corresponds to the knowing shaping, the third corresponds to the second, and the fourth corresponds to the third. This indicates the perfection of the power of the Lord, Exalted is He, and the conformity of what is decreed with what is known. So blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds, and the best of creators.

A parallel to this decree is the general writing before the creatures, and then the writing of what will happen from year to year on the Night of Decree (laylat al-qadr). Each of these stages is an elaboration of what precedes it and a diversification of it. The words of the Messenger of Allah confirm one another, explain one another, and agree with what exists in actuality, and do not contradict it. He only informs about what the senses and the intellect cannot independently grasp, not about what contradicts the senses and the intellect. What people know and can grasp independently is either a concrete matter upon which faith depends, or a legal ruling upon which obligation depends. And Allah knows best.

(Section)

If it is asked: Which organ is formed first before all the other organs?

It is said: Opinions differ on this in four views. The first is that it is the heart, which is the view of most scholars. The second is that it is the brain and the eyes, which is the view of Hippocrates (Buqrat). The third is that it is the liver, which is the view of Muhammad ibn Zakariyya (al-Razi). The fourth is that it is the navel, which is the view of a group of physicians.

The proponents of the heart said: There is no doubt that in the semen there is a spiritual power, and because of that power the person is made to become a human being. Its need for the spirit, which is the matter of the powers, is greater. Therefore, there must be a particular gathering place for that spirit from which it is sent out to the rest of the organs. So the spiritual substance is the first thing that is sent out from the semen and gathers in one place, and what reaches that spiritual substance from all sides surrounds it. Its gathering point must therefore be the center, and the rest of the parts surround it. That center is the heart.

They also said: The completion of the body depends on the innate heat by which the body lives, and the organ from which the innate power by which it grows must come first, and that is the heart.

They also said: The actions of the powers are completed only by the spirit, and the spirit must have something to which it attaches, and that to which it attaches must come before the powers, and that is the heart.

They also said: This is the most fitting and appropriate to the wisdom of the Lord, Exalted is He. The heart is a king and the organs are its soldiers and servants. When the heart is sound, its soldiers are sound, and when it is corrupt, they are corrupted. The Prophet (ﷺ) indicated in a sound hadith what points to this when he said: "Indeed, in the body there is a lump of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Verily, it is the heart." So how fitting is it that this lump should be first in existence before the rest that follow it, just as they follow it in soundness and corruption.

They also said: The anatomists have observed in the semen, when it has become a drop, that the heart is in its center.

The proponents of the brain said: We have observed in eggs that the first thing to form in the chicks is their head. And the way of Allah in the emergence of the fetus is that the first thing to appear of it into existence is its head.

The proponents of the liver said: Since the semen needs a nourishing power that increases its substance until it becomes such that the organs can form in it, the liver is the first and earliest of the organs to it, and it is the seat of the nourishing power.

The proponents of the navel said: The fetus's need to draw nourishment is greater than its need for food and perception, and it draws nourishment through the navel.

The first view is the most preferable among these opinions. The heart, its station, its nobility, and the place where Allah has set it, indicate that it is the one that begins before the other organs, preceding them in existence. And Allah knows best.

(Section)

If it is asked: Before the spirit is breathed into the fetus, did it have movement and sensation or not?

It is said: It had the movement of growth and nourishment, like plants. Its movement of growth and nourishment was not by will. When the spirit was breathed into it, the movement of its sensation and will was joined to its movement of growth and nourishment.

If it is said: It has been established that the child is formed from the water of both parents. Do they mix and blend until they become one water, or is one of them the matter and the other like the rennet that curdles it?

It is said: This is a matter about which the scholars of natural science have differed. A group of them said that the father's semen does not become part of the fetus; rather, it is the matter of the spirit that flows through the organs, and all the parts of the body are from the mother's semen. Others said that it is formed from the female's semen and then dissolves and decays.

They said: For this reason the child is a part of its mother, and for this reason the Law made it follow her in freedom and slavery.

They said: For this reason, if a man mounts the female slave of another man and she bears a child, the child belongs to the owner of the mother, not the owner of the stallion, because it was formed from her parts, her innards, her flesh, and her blood, and the father's water is like the water that irrigates the land.

They said: Sense perception witnesses that the parts in the newborn that come from its mother are many times more than the parts that come from its father. Therefore it is established that its formation is from the mother's semen and the menstrual blood, and the father's semen is the agent that curdles it, like the rennet.

The majority disputed this and said that it is formed from the semen of the man and the woman. Then they had two views:

One is that from the male's semen come its organs and parts, and from the female's semen its form. The second is that the organs, parts, and form were all formed from the combination of the two waters, and that the two mixed and blended and became one water. This is the correct view, because we find that form and shaping sometimes resemble the father and sometimes the mother. And Allah knows best.

This is indicated by the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿O mankind, We created you from a male and a female﴾. The origin is the male, for from him comes the seed, and from him comes the irrigation, while the female is a vessel and a repository for her offspring, which she nurtures in her womb as she nurtures it in her lap. For this reason the child belongs to the father in lineage and descent. As for its following the mother in freedom and slavery, that is because it was formed and became a child only in her womb, and she nourished it with her milk, together with the part of her that is in it. And the father has more right to its lineage and its paternal affiliation, because he is its origin, its matter, and its copy. And the one of them who is more noble in religion has more right to it, in favor of the religion of Allah and His Law.

If it is said: Why not extend this principle and say that if a man's seed falls into another man's land, the crop belongs to the owner of the land, not the owner of the seed?

It is said: The difference between them is that seed is a valuable property placed in the land of another, so it belongs to its owner, and he owes the rent of the land, or it is shared between them.
